Professor Nishant Kumar Verma , Chairperson of Career Development Services and faculty of the Production & Operations Management area, IIM Bangalore, said: “Despite being a challenging year for the job market around the world, IIM Bangalore conducted the process very efficiently. We are also glad to share that job offers made during the process have set a new benchmark, both in terms of the number of offers made and the diversity of roles across sectors. It is also a testament to the Institute’s collaborative relationship with the industry where both existing and new collaborations have been equally fruitful for all stakeholders.” Tapas Ranjan Pati, Head of Career Development Services, IIMB, said: “The IIM Bangalore Career Development Services team and the Student Placement Committee have demonstrated exceptional dedication, achieving a record number of job offers during the placement week. Leading global recruiters provided highly positive feedback on both the students’ performance and the seamless placement process.” Management Consulting remains the top career choice among students, accounting for 41% of the offers, followed by Technology/Product Management and Investment Banking. Other prominent sectors that recruited our MBA students include FMCG, Retail, E-commerce, Conglomerates, Fintech, Healthcare, and Manufacturing, spanning functions such as strategy, finance, marketing, general management, product management, operations, and analytics. According to the Student Placement Committee, “With the largest batch among all IIMs, this placement season witnessed strong participation from both legacy as well as new recruiters, with about 30% being first-time recruiters. We also secured 100-plus offers in the Lateral Placement Process (for candidates with more than 18 months of work experience), the highest among the top B-schools in India. This season stands as a testament to our Institute’s strong industry standing and the deep trust recruiters place in our students.” Top recruiters include Accenture Strategy (75), Boston Consulting Group (25), TCS Management Consulting (24), American Express (20), Bain & Company (17), PwC (16) and McKinsey & Company (14). Create Date 12 Mar Largest batch of 595 students at IIM Bangalore receive record 650+ offers Management Consulting remains the top career choice among students, accounting for 41% of the offers, followed by Technology/Product Management and Investment Banking 12 March 2025, Bengaluru: The Lateral and Final Placements for the PGP and PGPBA Class of 2023-25 of Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) saw all 595 students who appeared for placements being placed in 176 firms. Professor Nishant Kumar Verma , Chairperson of Career Development Services and faculty of the Production & Operations Management area, IIM Bangalore, said: “Despite being a challenging year for the job market around the world, IIM Bangalore conducted the process very efficiently. We are also glad to share that job offers made during the process have set a new benchmark, both in terms of the number of offers made and the diversity of roles across sectors. It is also a testament to the Institute’s collaborative relationship with the industry where both existing and new collaborations have been equally fruitful for all stakeholders.” Tapas Ranjan Pati, Head of Career Development Services, IIMB, said: “The IIM Bangalore Career Development Services team and the Student Placement Committee have demonstrated exceptional dedication, achieving a record number of job offers during the placement week. Leading global recruiters provided highly positive feedback on both the students’ performance and the seamless placement process.” Management Consulting remains the top career choice among students, accounting for 41% of the offers, followed by Technology/Product Management and Investment Banking. Other prominent sectors that recruited our MBA students include FMCG, Retail, E-commerce, Conglomerates, Fintech, Healthcare, and Manufacturing, spanning functions such as strategy, finance, marketing, general management, product management, operations, and analytics. According to the Student Placement Committee, “With the largest batch among all IIMs, this placement season witnessed strong participation from both legacy as well as new recruiters, with about 30% being first-time recruiters. We also secured 100-plus offers in the Lateral Placement Process (for candidates with more than 18 months of work experience), the highest among the top B-schools in India. This season stands as a testament to our Institute’s strong industry standing and the deep trust recruiters place in our students.” Top recruiters include Accenture Strategy (75), Boston Consulting Group (25), TCS Management Consulting (24), American Express (20), Bain & Company (17), PwC (16) and McKinsey & Company (14). title: IIMB - JJM | Jal Jeevan Mission | IIM Banglore
text: IIMB - JJM | Jal Jeevan Mission | IIM Banglore What We do We examine the economic aspects of water technology and utility and conduct evidence-based applied research through working papers, case studies, policy reports and policy dialogues. We analyse the sustainability of rural drinking water supply systems and evaluate the impact of the Jal Jeevan Mission on employment, health, and human capital formation. We also organise capacity-building workshops and policy seminars on issues related to rural drinking water management. The Jal Jeevan Mission Chair Professor Dr. Gopal Naik Professor Gopal Naik is the JJM Chair Professor at IIMB. He is also the Senior Fellow at the Centre for Public Policy at IIMB. He specializes in agricultural and environmental economics, rural development and technology adaption. A recipient of the DR. D.K. Desai and American Agricultural Economics Association Awards, he has advised several national and international organizations and contributed to key government policies. He has led the Unnat Bharath Abhiyan and the award-winning SAMIE tele-education project. Parameswaran Iyer talks about JJM Research at IIMB Parameswaran Iyer, former Secretary of the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation, led the Swachh Bharat Mission and initiated the Jal Jeevan Mission. As CEO of NITI Ayog (2022-2023), he has driven key national policies. Currently, he serves as Executive Director at the World Bank, representing South Asia. Hear his thoughts about us. text: Team | JJM | IIM Banglore Meet the Team Dr Gopal Naik Jal Jeevan Mission Chair Professor Professor Gopal Naik is the JJM Chair Professor at IIMB. He is also the Senior Fellow a t th e Centre for Public Policy at IIM B . P rof. Gopal Naik’s research focuses on agricultural and environmental economics , rural development , and technology adoption. He is the recipient of the Dr. D.K. Desai Award and the American Agricultural Economics Association Award. He has held consultancy positions in national and international organisations and has contributed significantly to government committees and policymaking. He also spearheaded the Unnat Bharath Abhiyan, and led the development of SAMIE, a tele-education project recognized with the WSIS 2015 Award. Dr Deepak Malghan A chemical engineer and ecological economist, Dr Deepak Malghan  is recognized for his work at the interface of scale theory and thermodynamics in ecological economics. His research focuses on the proportional relationship between the economy and the ecosystem, earning him accolades such as the 2015 VKRV Rao Prize in Social Sciences and the 2023 T N Khoshoo Memorial Award. Serving as an editor at Ecological Economics from 2018 to 2023, Dr Malghan has contributed to the field’s advancement. His affiliations with the Stockholm Environment Institute and his research on urban hydrology underscore his commitment to translational ecological economics. His lab at IIMB pioneers methods for analysing ethnic inequality and stratification, applying interdisciplinary tools to study ethnic politics and environmental injustice. of efficiency. Dr Aditya Shrinivas Dr Aditya Shrinivas specializes in development economics. His research focuses on food security, health, and nutrition outcomes. He has a Ph.D. in Applied Economics from the University of Illinois Urbana Champaign. M Rajendra Consultant M Rajendra was Administrative Officer at IIMB and was superannuated in 2020. Babita Kathayat Post Doctoral Research Associate Dr. Babita Kathayat is an agricultural economist who specializes in using quantitative data analysis and econometric research methods to inform evidence-based policy making that foster sustainable development and poverty reduction. Her research interests include sustainable agricultural systems, technology adoption, and promoting gender-responsive and socially inclusive development. She holds a Ph.D. in agricultural economics from ICAR-National Dairy Research Institute, Karnal. Previously, she contributed to research projects at CIMMYT and supported G20 policy negotiations at the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare. Esha Chakraborty Technical Assistant Esha Chakraborty is an IISc Bangalore certified data scientist with a specialized expertise in Geographic Information Systems. She completed her MTech. in Geomatics Engineering from IIT (ISM), Dhanbad. Her focus areas are data analysis, data visualization and gaining actionable insights from data. Ipsita Sarkar Senior Research Associate Ipsita holds a Master’s degree in Applied Economics from Christ University, Bengaluru. She has recently submitted her Ph.D. thesis for adjudication. Her area of interest lies in gender and labour economics. Prior to joining IIMB, she has gained experience in working as a researcher in Institute for Human Development, New Delhi. Anjali Dominic Technical Assistant Anjali Dominic is an environmental science postgraduate specializing in environmental impact assessment, water and soil quality analysis, and sustainable environmental management. Prior to joining IIM Bangalore, she worked at CSIR-NEERI contributing to projects on environmental monitoring, policy compliance, and pollution control. Her areas of interest lie in the intersection of environmental science, data-driven research, and public policy. Rishikaa Junior Research Associate Rishikaa is a post-graduate in Economics from TERI School of Advanced Studies. Her research interests lie in understanding how institutional frameworks and policy interventions influence community-level outcomes. Logesh A Junior Research Associate Logesh Arul holds a Master’s degree in Economics from Madras Christian College, with a focus on applied econometrics, quantitative economics, and public policy. Prior to joining IIM Bangalore, He worked at the Madras Institute of Development Studies on the Economic Valuation of Eco-System Services in Tamil Nadu’s wetlands.

text: Ongoing Studies | JJM | IIMB Ongoing Studies A Case Study of Yadgir district in Karnataka The objective was twofold – establish collaboration with Kalike, a Tata Trust organization, and identify and explore research gaps in the implementation of the JJM scheme in the region. To understand the status and implementation of JJM scheme in Jaunpur district, Purvanchal region of Uttar Pradesh The first field visit was conducted in three blocks- Shahganj, Suithakala, & Khutahan of Jaunpur district, UP. It is also proposed to do a comparative study between Yadgir district of Karnataka and Jaunpur district of Uttar Pradesh in the status & implementation of drinking water supply Operation and Maintenance of MVS system in Arsikere taluk of Karnataka The JJM-IIMB team studied the Gandasiulti Village Scheme (MVS) in Arsikere. It is one of the largest MVS schemes in Karnataka as it covers 143 villages.

title: Field visits | JJM | IIMB
text: Field visits | JJM | IIMB Field Visits Gokarna, Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka: Assessing the sustainability of multi-village drinking water supply systems This case study explores the progress of JJM in Gokarna MVS and covers six Gram Panchayats – Gokarna, Hiregutti, Bargi, Hanehalli, Nadumaskeri, and Torke. There are 19 villages in these six GPs, which receive water through MVS. Ganjam district, Odisha: Functioning of single village drinking water supply schemes This study explores the functioning of water supply systems in five villages in the district. It highlights the significance of institutional support (Gram Vikas, in this case) and the need for building community ownership. It also offers policy recommendations based on findings that support a demand-driven water supply strategy. Tumkuru district, Karnataka: Drinking water supply models for schools – Case Studies of JJM in providing safe and potable water The researchers examine WASH facilities in four schools and examine awareness among students before and after the intervention activities. They also suggest action plans for schools to enhance of the impact of WASH. Ujjain district, Madhya Pradesh: Rural area research study on water charges, collection, and O&M structure A reconnaissance survey was conducted to understand MVS and SVS functionality and operations in select villages in the district. The purpose of this visit was to understand how charges, under JJM, are calculated and collected from households. Jaunpur district, Uttar Pradesh: Challenges with implementing JJM A field visit was conducted to identify and explore the issues pertaining to the implementation of the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) scheme in this region

The seminar brought together researchers, academicians, and civil society for deliberations on water conservation, river and lake rejuvenation, and ecosystem preservation. title: Capacity Building | JJM | IIMB
text: Capacity Building | JJM | IIMB Capacity Building Online training programme on Financial Management of Piped Drinking Water Service Delivery Organization held from 26 th - 28 th December 2023 as a part of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) Professor Chair outreach and capacity building activities at IIMB. A three-day online training programme was conducted from 26th- 28th December 2023 on Financial Management of Piped Drinking Water Service Delivery Organization as a part of IIM Bangalore JJM professor chair outreach and capacity building activity. A total of 83 participants attended the online training programme. The course was held online (through ZOOM) consisting of three sessions of one hour each. Key objectives of the programme were to facilitate participants to understand the concepts and tools specifically developed for financial management of piped drinking water service and  to apply them to real world situations. Course Feedback Summary of the online training programme on Financial Management of Piped Drinking Water Service Delivery Organization held from 26 th - 28 th December 2023 as a part of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) Professor Chair outreach and capacity building activities at IIMB. Session 1 The training programme on Financial Management of Piped Drinking Water Service Delivery Organization covers various aspects such as the importance of financial management, the role of community ownership in cost recovery, conceptual underpinning in pricing, pricing strategy, costing methods, and illustration of case studies for multi village scheme, single village scheme and in-village distribution systems. It emphasizes the role of community participation in managing piped drinking water supply and the need for community ownership to ensure sustainability. It discusses the involvement of communities in infrastructure development, planning, implementation, and operations, as well as the determination of user charges for financial sustainability. This course provides an overview starting with the need for pricing piped drinking water, setting up user charges, discussing pricing methods - including cost-based, competition-based, and value-based pricing, followed by the determination of the demand and the supply. It also highlights how different market structures affect pricing. Water being a public good and an essential commodity, underlines the necessity to prioritize social welfare over profit. The course explores the different market structure and advocates for cost based pricing and competitive market pricing principles for determining user charges. Session 2 The second session discusses the role of pricing principles and tariff mechanisms for determining prices. It focuses on volumetric pricing and flat pricing strategies further delving into the three categories of volumetric pricing- uniform water tariff, two-part tariff and Increasing block tariff mechanisms. It illustrates the relationship between costs and demand and highlights the situations of low demand for piped drinking water system and recommends ways to correct the issue of low demand. It highlights the importance of full cost computation which is needed to be done even if the immediate objective is to cover only operational costs through user charges as it helps in understanding the total cost of service delivery and plan for meeting replacement expenses well ahead of time so that the burden of lumpsum expenses can be avoided. The course also discusses how perception plays a role in low demand of piped drinking water and how quality water availability is a pivotal factor in it. It briefly discusses the social costs and benefits of providing piped drinking water service. Session 3 The third session explores the different types of cost- Capital expenditure and Operational expenditure. It emphasizes the importance of understanding costs and computing capital costs and O&M cost for recovering them using user charges. It also focuses on time value of money and the pivotal role it plays in arriving at annualized fixed cost. It advocates for considering amortization rather than depreciation while calculating annualized fixed cost because depreciation alone cannot take care of full fixed cost as it only accounts for the book value of the capital cost. Further it demonstrates the steps involved in cost calculation of multi village scheme, single village scheme and in-village distribution system using the case studies from Gokarna and Odisha. Illustration of cost calculation for MVS and IVDS in Gokarna has been done by computing the Capital expenditure for both MVS and IVDS in Gokarna and calculating the individual O&M for MVS and SVS of Gokarna. Computation of capital and O&M cost for SVS has also been demonstrated. At the end of cost computation determination of surplus/deficit of piped drinking water system is being illustrated using an Excel template which contains the formulas for cost computation for MVS, IVDS and SVS. This template can be used for cost computation of different schemes. The template is useful in managing the finances and can be used by the members of the GP and VWSC to understand the minimum user charge for recovering the full cost of delivering piped drinking water to households. The Key Takeaways Importance of Financial Management: Emphasizes the significance of community participation and ownership in managing piped drinking water supply for sustainability. Cost Recovery: Highlights the need for determining user charges to ensure financial sustainability and efficient water delivery system. Pricing Principles: Discusses cost-based, competition-based, and value-based pricing principles, and their implications on water supply and demand. Costing Methods: Provides insights into capital costs, operating expenses, and the importance of understanding the full cost of servicing water delivery. Unit Cost Computation: Illustrates practical steps for computing unit costs and emphasizes the relationship between costs and demand. Costs and Revenue: Covers the determination of water charges, market structures, and the relationship between marginal revenue, marginal cost, and profit maximization. Overall, the presentation aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of financial management, cost recovery, pricing principles, and practical illustrations in the context of piped drinking water service delivery organizations. Policy Directions Efficient financial management at the VWSC level requires policy direction on the following: Whether states budget support is available for meeting operations and maintenance cost of MVS? Whether state budget support is available for repair and replacement of assets either at MVS level or SVS level? What is the nature of funding support available to SVS on technical assistance needed, training, skill development and capacity building? Whether the State budget will be available for replacement of assets at the end of the life span of those assets. If so, what is the extent of support? Whether state budget support will be available for water quality testing expenses incurred by VWSC? Whether state budget support is available to meet the electricity charges of SVS? Whether state budget support is available to meet the investment on solar pumps Topics Links Financial Training programme course slides Financial Management course slides Excel template for cost computation of MVS and SVS Excel Template for cost computation of MVS and SVS Keywords and guidelines for using the template Keywords and guidelines for using the Excel Template Assignment Task: Applying the concepts and getting the opportunity to do cost computation Assignment Task A three-day online training programme was conducted from 26th- 28th December 2023 on Financial Management of Piped Drinking Water Service Delivery Organization as a part of IIM Bangalore JJM professor chair outreach and capacity building activity. A total of 83 participants attended the online training programme. The course was held online (through ZOOM) consisting of three sessions of one hour each. Key objectives of the programme were to facilitate participants to understand the concepts and tools specifically developed for financial management of piped drinking water service and to apply them to real world situations. Session 1 covers various aspects such as pricing, community ownership, and case studies. It emphasizes community participation in managing piped drinking water supply and advocates for cost-based pricing principles. Session 2 discusses pricing principles and tariff mechanisms for determining prices. It highlights the importance of full cost computation and the social costs and benefits of providing piped drinking water service. Session 3 The third session discusses the importance of understanding costs and computing capital and O&M costs. It advocates for considering amortization rather than depreciation while calculating annualized fixed cost. The session also demonstrates the steps involved in cost calculation of different schemes and provides an Excel template for cost computation.

title: Jal Jeevan Mission and UNICEF host state-level write-shop on Asset Handover Guidelines at IIMB  | JJM | IIMB
text: Jal Jeevan Mission and UNICEF host state-level write-shop on Asset Handover Guidelines at IIMB  | JJM | IIMB Jal Jeevan Mission and UNICEF host state-level write-shop on Asset Handover Guidelines at IIMB On 22 and 23 October, local government representatives united to strengthen community water management across Karnataka 5 November, 2024, Bengaluru: The Jal Jeevan Mission Office at IIM Bangalore, in partnership with the UNICEF-Hyderabad Field Office hosted a Two-day State level Write-shop on 22 and 23 October 2024 on ‘Developing Guidelines on the Handover Process of JJM Assets to Gram Panchayats and VWSCs in Karnataka’. Bridging existing gaps in the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) asset handover process, the two-day write-shop brought a diverse spectrum of field experiences to the forefront. The collaborative initiative aimed to identify critical challenges, explore rapid appraisal findings, and map solutions to shape a robust framework for asset transfer. A write-shop was thus proposed to engage key stakeholders in a dialogue and knowledge transfer for an effective handover process, ensuring sustainable management of JJM assets. This Write-shop welcomed over 80 diverse stakeholders including Government representatives such as the Commissioner, Panchayat Raj, Director of RDWSD, as well as other key officials from these departments. Members of local government including Gram Panchayat members, Panchayat Development Officers, selected members of Village Water and Sanitation Committee (VWSC), civil society representatives including Community-Based Organizations (CBOs) and Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) joined forces with technical and financial experts from the sector, contributing valuable insights and expertise. The write-shop employed a participatory approach, combining expert presentations, panel discussions, group work, and case studies. Guided by skilled moderators, participants from across Karnataka shared their experiences, highlighted present challenges, and exchanged best practices for asset handover. The collective knowledge-sharing process is set to shape a standardized framework and refined guidelines for an efficient, sustainable handover of JJM assets to Gram Panchayats and their communities. Additionally, the write-shop’s outcomes will lay the groundwork for capacity-building initiatives, empowering communities to manage and maintain effective water supply systems.

title: Workshop on Operation & Maintenance of States pertaining to Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)  | JJM | IIMB
text: Workshop on Operation & Maintenance of States pertaining to Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)  | JJM | IIMB Workshop on Operation & Maintenance of States pertaining to Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) The JJM Office at IIM Bangalore, in collaboration with UNICEF, hosted a national Consultative Workshop on JJM Operations and Maintenance (O&M) on 24th August, 2024. In his opening address, Prof. Gopal Naik, JJM Chair Professor at IIM Bangalore, highlighted the Jal Jeevan Mission’s significance, underlining its role as a model for public service delivery. With an estimated total cost of Rs. 3.6 lakh crore, JJM has dramatically improved rural water supply infrastructure, which in turn has contributed to public health improvements, employment opportunities, and educational advancements for girls. However, challenges in operations and maintenance (O&M) and water quality persist, necessitating community involvement and innovative financial management strategies. The JJM Office at IIM Bangalore has been actively addressing these challenges by developing frameworks on economics of supply as well as operations and maintenance, and collaborating with various organizations. Dr. Chandra Bhushan Kumar, Additional Secretary and Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission, emphasized the historical importance of water management in India and the significant progress made by JJM, which, he said, had increased water access from 16% to 78% in five years. He highlighted the need for sustainable O&M practices, urging state governments as well as communities to reconnect with traditional water management methods while adapting them for modern use. A draft Operation and Maintenance Policy was circulated at the workshop and discussed with the participating states. Presentations were made by the states, showcasing their O&M strategies related to rural water supply. Tamil Nadu has implemented Single Village Schemes (SVS) and Combined Water Supply Schemes (CWSS), transferring services to village panchayats. The state faces challenges in user charge collection. Village and panchayat bodies have been asked to collect minimal local tariffs, but there remains a significant gap between the costs and the tariffs collected. Tamil Nadu also utilizes advanced technologies like IoT and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) for water quality monitoring and management. Kerala ’s water management is overseen by the Kerala Water Authority (KWA), which employs the Blue Brigade system and Kudumbashree women for O&M. The state faces a financial gap between O&M costs and water tariffs, which it plans to address through revised tariffs and increased efficiency. Kerala also focuses on digital transformation, with all services available online, and employs GIS for asset management. In Karnataka , a volumetric tariff system has been introduced, with annual increases to cover O&M costs. The state emphasizes capacity building and asset management, with a focus on upgrading service delivery and monitoring water supply through IoT. Grievance redressal is managed by Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (RDPR). Maharashtra , reliant on groundwater resources, faces sustainability challenges. The state has drafted an O&M policy and plans to appoint Jal Surakshaks at the gram panchayat level to manage water supply. Maharashtra is also focusing on skill development and ensuring water availability through geo-tagged assets and regular water quality testing. Andhra Pradesh is focused on shifting from groundwater-dependent sources like borewells to more sustainable surface water-based schemes, particularly Multi Village Schemes (MVS). A robust O&M policy tailored for different types of water supply schemes is needed. Significant contributions from L&T and the Sathya Sai Trust have improved O&M efficiency, particularly for MVS. The state aims to increase MVS coverage from the current 45% of rural households. In Madhya Pradesh , MVS coverage is low at less than 10%, but efforts are underway to expand it to 230-250 villages, ensuring sustainable water sources for both MVS and Single Village Schemes (SVS). High energy and manpower costs are a challenge, and renewable energy projects like solar power are being considered to reduce these costs. Equitable water use from Overhead Tanks (OHTs) and greater transparency at the Panchayat level are emphasized. In Telangana , Mission Bhagiratha is a key initiative providing surface water from the Krishna and Godavari rivers, with an O&M policy under review. The project targets 100 litres per capita per day (LPCD) for rural areas and 150 LPCD for urban areas. Funding comes from both government spending and revenue from commercial connections, with ongoing training for local officials. The state has achieved 100% coverage of Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTCs) under JJM, and all assets have been geo-mapped for monitoring. In Rajasthan , O&M strategies differ between SVS and MVS, with responsibilities divided between Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs) and external agencies. Significant costs are associated with electricity consumption for tubewells, and Nal Jal Mitras have been appointed to manage O&M, though some gaps remain. Consumers must meet specific conditions to avail of tap water connections, and GIS mapping is used for asset management. In Gujarat , despite a high achievement in potable water supply before JJM, challenges in O&M persist, particularly regarding community ownership and funding. The panchayats face difficulties in collecting user fees and managing funds, with a need for better community engagement and external support. After the state presentations, Prof. Gopal Naik again emphasized the importance of sustainable water use and community-managed O&M, where local entities like Gram Panchayats and VWSCs play a crucial role. Different operational models include community-managed, state-centric with community ownership, and external agency support, each with varying levels of community involvement. Financing for O&M includes user fees, establishing water tariffs, and setting up corpus funds for major repairs, with a focus on capacity building and training for local communities. State-level support is vital for major repairs, water quality testing, and financial planning, while local bodies manage day-to-day operations. Manish Wasuja, Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene Specialist at UNICEF India, highlighted the crucial role states play in the operation and maintenance (O&M) of the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), a scheme that is closely linked to children’s health. While states are at varying stages of policy development, the Ministry of Jal Shakti has created a national O&M framework, and UNICEF can assist states in drafting or reviewing policies to overcome challenges. Emphasis was placed on ensuring source sustainability through rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge, along with decentralized and centralized O&M models for Single Village Schemes (SVS) and Multi-Village Schemes (MVS). Financing O&M involves routine maintenance, energy charges management, flexible user charges, and tapping into financial resources like the 15th Finance Commission grants. Capacity building is essential, involving collaboration between Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and skilled local resources. Water quality monitoring, supported by NABL-accredited labs, is critical, alongside quick response protocols for contamination. Pradeep Singh, Director of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Government of India, suggested leveraging political leadership to monitor JJM’s progress. He spoke of the significant investment of INR 45-50 billion under the Har Ghar Jal mission but said gaps existed in monitoring water service delivery. To address this, the Government of India plans to develop a Water Supply Monitoring App for real-time tracking of water supply across 600,000 villages. The proposed app will allow users to report service disruptions, with data feeding into monthly reviews to monitor and resolve issues efficiently. The process involves nominating village-level individuals to report water supply information via the app, which will enhance transparency and accountability in water service delivery. This initiative is expected to improve the effectiveness of the Jal Jeevan Mission by ensuring continuous monitoring and timely corrective actions. The session concluded with discussions that urged for a renewed focus towards enhancing O&M, enhancing community management and building capacity at the local level for sustainability of rural drinking water supply schemes.

Read More >> About IIMB The Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) believes in building leaders through holistic, transformative and innovative education Read More >> IIMB, World Bank and RDWSD hosted a focused discussion on ‘Challenges and Solutions for Sustainable Water Supply’ on June 19 The session explored key issues in rural water governance and strategies for sustainable, equitable water access 20 JUNE, 2025: The Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM ) at IIMB, in collaboration with the World Bank Team and the Rural Drinking Water and Sanitation Department (RDWSD), Government of Karnataka, hosted a focused discussion on ‘Challenges and Solutions for Sustainable Water Supply’ on June 19, 2025, at IIMB. The event began with a welcome address and opening remarks by Prof. Gopal Naik, Chairperson, JJM at IIMB, who set the context by emphasising the growing need for collaborative, evidence-based solutions to strengthen rural water supply systems. Mr. Jafar Shareef Sutar , Deputy Secretary (Admin), RDWSD, Government of Karnataka, shared key initiatives currently being implemented by the department to improve infrastructure, enhance service delivery, and promote institutional coordination for reliable and inclusive access to drinking water in rural regions. The World Bank team , led by Sumila Gulyani , Water Practice Head, South Asia, along with Kristoffer Welsien , Mariappa Kullappa , and Aroha Bahuguna , presented their observations on ensuring sustainability in rural water services. The team stressed that reliable access to water requires not just physical infrastructure, but robust operational systems, continuous capacity building, behavioural change, and strong local technical leadership. Setting the tone for deeper collaboration, the session facilitated dialogue between policymakers, development practitioners, and researchers on practical solutions to address on-ground challenges especially those related to Operation and Maintenance (O&M), governance structures, and data-driven decision-making. This event marked another milestone in IIMB’s efforts to foster impactful dialogue on public policy and rural development through multi-stakeholder engagement. text: IIMBx – About Us | Digital Learning & Online Programs × About IIMBx IIMBx Digital Learning Foundation, the digital learning initiative of the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB), was established to provide world-class education to learners everywhere, regardless of financial, academic, or social circumstances. title: AI For Managers Program - IIMBx
text: AI For Managers Program - IIMBx × Professional Certificate in Artificial Intelligence for Managers Apply Now FAQ 7  Programme Objectives  Who Can Apply?  Courses Offered Important Dates About the Programme The Certificate Program in Artificial Intelligence for Managers is a 10-month, fully online program designed to equip professionals with the knowledge and skills required to understand, apply, and lead AI initiatives in their organizations. Unlike technical AI courses, this programme is specifically curated for managers and decision-makers who need to bridge the gap between data science teams and business strategy. Participants will not only learn the underlying concepts of AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Generative AI , but also develop the ability to evaluate opportunities, assess risks, and design business solutions powered by AI. This programme is structured around 8 sequential modules , ensuring a smooth progression from foundational concepts to advanced applications, supported by hands-on tools like Python, SPSS, Excel, and Tableau . By integrating Harvard Business Publishing case studies , peer-to-peer discussions, and practical assignments, the programme fosters experiential learning that goes beyond classroom theory. It also includes continuous assessments ensuring that learners get certified with both conceptual clarity and applied expertise. On successful completion, learners will earn a Professional Certificate from IIM Bangalore —one of India’s top-ranked management institutions—joining a network of high-achieving alumni across industries. Important Dates  Registrations Open 30th August 2025  Registration Close 15th November 2025  Course Orientation 28th November 2025 Chandrashekhar Mane PMP Based on my experience I found the course content to be very relevant & is an attempt to democratize Artificial Intelligence knowledge and bridge gap between industry & academy. I would urge all aspirants to embark on this long, exciting & fulfilling journey unravelling AI mystic in august company of Prof Dinesh Kumar, Prof Manranjan Pradhan (Python & MLOps) , Prof Rajluxmy (Prescriptive Analytics) & Prof Naveen Bhansali (Deep Learning) ably supported by Ms Seema Jaiswal who has done wonderful job of coordinating with students and Professors. In particular Deep Learning, ML Ops & Prescriptive Analytics modules have been top class & content was curated to give insights to practical aspects. In personal capacity, I have learnt a lot and this course has helped me in joining dots during evaluating business requirements, conceptualizing & architecting solutions. Programme Objectives Z Grasp the Business Value of AI – Understand how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning are reshaping industries, competition, and organizational strategies. Z Build Strong Foundations in Data Science – Develop a clear understanding of data handling, statistical methods, and analytical models that form the backbone of AI applications. Z Apply Advanced Analytics – Use descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive techniques to address real-world business challenges and drive informed decision-making. Z Leverage Machine Learning Effectively – Implement supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning algorithms to solve diverse business problems. Z Master AI Technologies – Gain hands-on knowledge of Artificial Neural Networks, Deep Learning frameworks (CNNs, RNNs, LSTM, Transformers), and Generative AI models for practical applications. Z Tell Stories with Data – Transform data into meaningful insights using visualization, dashboards, and storytelling techniques for managerial impact. Z Develop Technical Proficiency – Work confidently with tools such as Python, SPSS, Excel, and Tableau to analyze, visualize, and deploy AI-driven solutions. Z Drive AI Adoption Responsibly – Evaluate ethical considerations, risks, and opportunities in AI deployment to ensure responsible and sustainable use of technology. Who Can Apply Ideal for: Mid-career and senior managers looking to integrate AI into strategic roles Consultants, IT professionals, and project managers steering AI/ML initiatives Entrepreneurs seeking to leverage AI for innovation and competitive scalability Eligibility Requirements: Minimum 3 years of professional experience Graduate degree in any discipline—management, engineering, science, or relevant fields Clear interest in applying AI/ML to solve business challenges and elevate decision-making Evaluation, Grading policy and Certification Evaluation, Grading policy and Certification Evaluation will be done using end of week assessments and final exam of all the courses. Assessments will be in online mode for all courses Participants are expected to score a minimum of 60% in all courses for successful completion of the program Programme Highlights Learn from Distinguished Faculty of a Premier B-School Study Anytime, Anywhere with Our Online Delivery Affiliate Alumni status of IIM Bangalore Case-Focused Curriculum Courses Offered Foundation of Data Science Speak data with confidence. Data Visualization and Story Telling Turn numbers into boardroom influence. Predictive Analysis Forecast outcomes that guide strategy. Machine Learning with Business Applications See algorithms in action on real business problems. Machine Learning using Python Practical skills to engage with technical teams. Artificial Neural Network and Deep Learning Understand the power behind modern AI. Reinforcement Learning Lead in dynamic, uncertain environments. Generative AI Harness the innovation of ChatGPT, LLMs & beyond. Faculty Dinesh Kumar U Sharada Sringeswara Manaranjan Pradhan Naveen Kumar Bhansali Slider Example Testimonials Ankita Umesh Panchariya This course was an incredible journey, unveiling the intricate world of algorithms, Machine Learning, and Neural Networks. From theory to hands-on projects, it expanded my understanding and ignited my passion for the limitless possibilities of AI. Rohit Chourey I am IT professional and working as Manager in Capgemini. I have 10 years of industry experience. I always wanted to learn how AI works and how to apply it in real world. But was not sure which course to attend. I compared this course with all course in market and came to conclusions to select this course as this holds best curriculum. Foundation and statistics module eye opening and benificial. This you will not get in any other course as detailed as in this course. I have started to apply all applications in my organisation, thanks IIMB Aditya Shankar This program’s comprehensive curriculum covered a range of cutting-edge topics, including Artificial Neural Networks, Reinforcement Learning, Prescriptive & Predictive Analytics, MLOps to name a few. I also found the module on visualization & Story telling very appropriate, as in roles as managers, it is critical to be able to be build trust with senior leadership via persuasive and convincing communications regarding the application of AI technologies in the organization. I wholeheartedly recommend this certification program to all managers who wish to future-proof their careers and lead their organizations into the AI-driven era. It is an investment that pays dividends by empowering you to harness the immense potential of AI and drive innovation, efficiency, and success in your respective domains. Saurabh Chaturvedi AI is a challenging topic but since the program was meant specially for managers, I felt encouraged to take up this 16 months endeavour. Prof. Dinesh Kumar, who leads this course, is one of the best in the field of AI. His teaching style and vast knowledge from real life case studies made the course very productive. The most complex of topics were delivered effortlessly by Prof. Dinesh and rest of the faculty. The course is very well structured – the first module, Foundations of Data Science, is really the backbone of the whole course. The modules are sequenced quite logically, given the vast nature of this field. All concepts are covered to a meaningful extent and through case studies and graded assignments, we were encouraged to learn further and internalise the topics. The course strikes a great balance between recorded lectures, live online and in-person sessions. This program has really equipped me to apply the learnings to my day to day job in the area of supply chain planning. I would highly recommended this program to people who are getting started with AI or are existing practitioners but want to revamp themselves by learning from the best in the industry. Syamkumar Rajasekharan Nair The rapid integration of AI technologies into various industries motivated me to join the AI for Managers program. Understanding the fundamentals of machine learning algorithms and their applications provided me with the confidence to engage in meaningful discussions with data scientists and engineers within my company. The insights into natural language processing were particularly eye-opening, as I realized the vast potential of AI-driven language technologies for customer engagement and sentiment analysis. Since completing the program, I have been able to apply my new found knowledge in various real-world scenarios. For instance, I have initiated an AI team within my Line of Business and bring multiple use cases which creates business Impact. This initiative not only started working on new projects also a created high-level motivation for the team to work on new technical topic. Furthermore, understanding the ethical implications of AI has allowed me to advocate for responsible AI practices within our organization, ensuring that we uphold the highest standards when handling data and deploying AI-driven solutions.In conclusion, the AI for Managers program has been a transformative experience for me. I highly recommend this program to any manager seeking to enhance their leadership skills and stay at the forefront of the AI revolution.. title: Faculty Development Program Demo: Teaching Excellence
text: Faculty Development Program Demo: Teaching Excellence × Faculty Development Program Registrations Closed Excellence in Learner-centric Pedagogy The Faculty Development Programme (FDP) on Creating Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) , organized by the IIMB Digital Learning Team, is designed to equip faculty members with the skills and knowledge required to design, develop, and deliver high-quality MOOCs. The FDP is structured into two parts: a one-day on-campus workshop on 26th April 2025 at IIM Bangalore, followed by a 45-day online training programme starting from 28th April 2025 . The programme covers the entire lifecycle of a MOOC — from planning and designing to production, delivery, and post-course activities. Through engaging content that includes short videos, text modules, and interviews with IIM Bangalore faculty members, participants will gain practical insights into MOOC development. By the end of the FDP, participants will be able to apply effective blended learning methodologies, design and produce engaging course content, and successfully manage the delivery of MOOCs. The on-campus workshop will introduce participants to MOOC development and blended learning methodologies, followed by hands-on practice in planning and storyboarding. The online component will provide in-depth knowledge on online pedagogy, content creation, learner engagement, and post-course evaluation, culminating in a capstone project where participants will create a mini MOOC.. text: SWAYAM | IIMBx | Ministry of Human Resource Development India × SWAYAM SWAYAM – Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds – is an initiative by the Ministry of Human Resource Development, Government of India, to offer online courses to learners across the country. IIMB is the coordinating institute for management education for SWAYAM Explore Courses Download Brochure Submit Proposal Introduction SWAYAM Programme was established under the aegis of the Ministry of Human Resources Development, Government of India, for expanding educational access and opportunities courses and pedagogies. Swayam courses cover all subjects and skill sectors from high school to higher education. SWAYAM seeks to bridge the digital divide for students who have hitherto remained untouched by the digital revolution and have not been able to join the mainstream of the knowledge economy. SWAYAM designed to achieve the three cardinal principles of Education Policy viz., access, equity and quality. Enrolments Open For July 2025 Semester REGISTER Why Choose Swayam? Through SWAYAM integrated learning platform courses from India’s top-ranking institutions and faculty are made available to learners anywhere in an asynchronous mode. All courses on the Swayam platform are free. Learners, if they are students currently enrolled in an educational institution or university, have also the option of transferring credits earned through the SWAYAM courses to their respective home institutions. Objective The objective of SWAYAM effort is to take the best teaching learning resources to all, including the most disadvantaged. To bridge the digital divide for students who have hitherto remained untouched by the digital revolution and have not been able to join the mainstream of the knowledge economy To provide one-stop web and mobile based interactive e-content for all courses from High School to University level To provide high quality learning experience using multimedia on an anytime, anywhere basis To provide state of the art system that allows easy access, monitoring and certification To provide peer interaction and discussion forum to clarify doubts. Submit MOOC Proposal Expression of Interest (MOOC Proposals) are invited from those who wish to offer online course(s) on the SWAYAM platform in the area of management. Interested Institutions and Universities can apply by sending a detailed MOOC proposal. As a National Coordinator, IIMB receives and evaluates MOOC (Massive Open Online Course) proposals in the area of management studies from Universities and Institutions willing to offer their course on SWAYAM. Universities and Institutions can send the proposals to IIMBx, the digital learning division of IIM Bangalore. title: PCHM Valedictory Ceremony for Karnataka Govt Doctors
text: PCHM Valedictory Ceremony for Karnataka Govt Doctors × Valedictory Ceremony of PCHM Programme for Karnataka Government Doctors by IIMBx Our Professional Certificate in Hospital Management is a well-crafted 12-month online program. It aims to equip professionals working in the healthcare industry with various leadership competencies such as managing people, innovations, organizational design, and developing strategies. Furthermore, it also emphasizes building managerial expertise in various areas such as operations, marketing, finance, and economics and an understanding of the regulatory framework of healthcare in India. The programme was started as a part social impact activity by IIMB through its digital learning initiative, IIMBx. We are happy to have been able to be a part of this batch, as this also serves one of our mottos of giving back to the society. We had enrolment of 15 learners, and the entire programme was run for them exclusively. The event marked a significant milestone in IIMBx’s commitment to driving social impact through accessible, high-quality education. The learners were assisted throughout the course, and recently, batch 1 was completed, and we proudly hosted the valedictory ceremony for the Public Health & Hospital Management (PCHM) programme tailored for public sector doctors of the Government of Karnataka. The event was graced by our esteemed leaders Prof. Rishikesha Krishnan, Director, IIMB; Prof. Vasanthi Srinivasan, Director, IIMBx; Mr. Sitaraman Shankar, CEO, IIMBx; and Prof. Vandana Singhvi Patel, Academic Director. This special cohort comprised 15 dedicated medical professionals who successfully completed the rigorous program with flying colors. Their outstanding performance is a testament to their dedication and the value of continuous professional development in the public health sector. We are sure that with this programme these senior doctors will now make an impact in their respective departments, further amplifying the impact of the program on both their careers and the healthcare system at large. Their advancement stands as a proud achievement for both the learners and the IIMBx faculty and staff who mentored them throughout the journey. The valedictory function was not just a celebration of academic achievement but also of collaboration between premier academic institutions and the public health machinery, working together to create meaningful, lasting change.

title: Faculty Development Programme 2025: Digital Excellence
text: Faculty Development Programme 2025: Digital Excellence × Faculty Development Programme 2025: A Journey Towards Digital Excellence by iimbx tech | May 1, 2025 | What's New We hope this message finds you well. We’re excited to share the story of our recent Faculty Development Programme (FDP) with you. If you’ve heard about it before, you’ll enjoy this deeper look. And if you haven’t—don’t worry, here’s a quick summary to catch you up! Overview The Faculty Development Programme (FDP) on Creating Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), organized by the IIMBx Digital Learning Team, is designed to help faculty members build the skills needed to design, develop, and deliver high-quality MOOCs. The FDP has two parts: A one-day on-campus workshop that took place on 26th April 2025 at IIM Bangalore, and A 45-day online training programme, which started on 28th April 2025. The theme for this year’s FDP was “Empowering Educators for the Digital Future.” We’re thrilled that we could contribute towards empowering educators through a series of engaging sessions on different topics. Inaugural Session The day began on a high note with an inspiring inaugural address by Mr. Sitaraman Shankar, CEO of IIMBx, followed by a warm and thoughtful opening remark from Prof. Rishikesha Krishnan, Director of IIMB. Their words truly set the tone for the day! Panel Discussions Moderated by Prof. Rishikesha Krishnan, the panel on “Innovations in Teaching – Classroom, Blended, and Online” featured insightful contributions from Prof. Ananth Krishnamurthy, Prof. Soudeep Deb, and Prof. Vandana Singhvi Patel. The discussion covered course design, integrating digital tools with human elements to enhance student engagement, and the evolving role of AI in education. Thought-provoking questions from faculty participants added great value to the session. SANGAM Launch Following the panel discussion, we launched SANGAM, our digital learning community. The excitement among participants was palpable as they explored new opportunities for collaboration and peer learning across institutions. Digital Pedagogues Session The session titled “Digital Pedagogues: Architects of the New Learning Era,” moderated by Prof. Vasanthi Srinivasan, featured six panelists who shared their unique perspectives on teaching in today’s digital age. It was a refreshing and eye-opening conversation. Key Talk and Reflection Post-lunch, Prof. Sridhar Iyer delivered an insightful talk on “From Research to Practice: The Digital Transformation of Education.” In this session, he shared valuable perspectives on the learner-centric MOOC model — an interactive approach designed to keep learners engaged throughout the course. Prof. Iyer also highlighted the ongoing shift from traditional pedagogies to 21st-century teaching practices, urging educators to rethink and redesign their methods to meet the evolving needs of today’s learners. To wrap up the learning sessions, Prof. Vasanthi Srinivasan led a heartfelt session on “Reflections on Teaching and Being a Teacher.” It was a poignant reminder of the passion and purpose behind the teaching profession. Digital Playbook & Closing Ceremony Before concluding the day, we introduced the Digital Learning Playbook, ensuring all participants felt confident about integrating it into their teaching practices. The valedictory session and certificate distribution marked a wonderful end to the day. Seeing the room filled with happy, satisfied faces was truly a rewarding moment for Team IIMBx. We are deeply grateful for the energy, passion, and enthusiasm that each participant brought to the FDP. Here’s to many more milestones in empowering educators for the digital future!

title: AI for Managers Batch 3 Begins In-Campus Journey
text: AI for Managers Batch 3 Begins In-Campus Journey × A Memorable First In-Campus Session for AI for Managers Batch-3 at IIMBx Hello everyone! We’re back with yet another exciting update from IIMBx. February 2025 was a particularly eventful month for us, and we couldn’t be more thrilled to share the highlights with you. As many of you already know, our AI for Managers Batch-2 learners had their much-anticipated valedictory ceremony this month. But what made the day even more special? The fact that our AI for Managers Batch-3 learners had their very first in-campus session on the same day! This wasn’t just a happy coincidence—it was a well-thought-out plan. We wanted our new batch to witness the celebratory atmosphere of the valedictory event and be inspired by their peers who had successfully completed the program. Seeing Batch-2 learners receive their certificates and bid farewell with pride and joy would undoubtedly serve as motivation for Batch-3 learners to stay committed and complete their journey successfully. Behind the Scenes: Planning and Preparation Of course, making sure everything went smoothly required meticulous planning. The IIMBx team put in a lot of effort to ensure a seamless experience, and special credit goes to Vijayalakshmi and Dimple for handling the intricate details. We had several rounds of meetings, strategized work allocations, and coordinated every aspect of the event to perfection. The Big Day: February 15th, 2025 The much-awaited day finally arrived! We welcomed over 120 learners from AI for Managers Batch-2 for their last session, while 70 learners out of the 131-cohort of Batch-3 joined us for their very first in-campus experience, and the rest of them joined on Zoom to attend the session online. The excitement was palpable—Batch-3 learners were eager to step onto the IIMB campus and immerse themselves in the learning environment. Their first session was with none other than Professor Dinesh Kumar , our program director. The day was structured into three engaging sessions. The first session involved an interactive discussion on a case study, led by Prof. Dinesh. The learners found it incredibly insightful and appreciated the deep dive into real-world applications of AI in management. The subsequent sessions were hands-on, allowing learners to apply their knowledge practically. The energy in the room was electric, with participants fully engaged and eager to learn. A Smoothly Executed Event & A Fitting Farewell Kudos to the entire IIMBx team for executing the event flawlessly! From coordinating logistics to ensuring the learners had the best possible experience, every detail was taken care of. The valedictory ceremony, scheduled for 6 PM , was a grand affair. Since the sessions wrapped up before the ceremony, the Batch-3 learners had time to explore the IIMB campus , soaking in its vibrant atmosphere. Many took the opportunity to visit the IIMB store , indulging in some souvenir shopping to commemorate their first visit. As the sun set, the valedictory event commenced. Batch-2 learners celebrated their achievements, sharing heartfelt reflections on their journey. The experience was inspiring for Batch-3, who left the event with renewed enthusiasm and determination to see their program through to completion. A Great Start & A Happy Goodbye All in all, February 15th, 2025, was a day to remember —a wonderful beginning for AI for Managers Batch-3 and a proud farewell for Batch-2. Seeing the enthusiasm, camaraderie, and sheer excitement among the learners was incredibly fulfilling. We can’t wait to see how Batch 3 progresses. Stay tuned for more updates, and until next time, happy learning!

title: BBA DBE First Term Exams Successfully Concluded
text: BBA DBE First Term Exams Successfully Concluded × Well Begun: BBA DBE First Term Exams Successfully Concluded! The Bachelor of Business Administration in Digital Business and Entrepreneurship (BBA-DBE) program seamlessly blends digital technology, business management, and entrepreneurship, preparing future leaders for the digital economy. This exclusive online degree program offers undergraduates the opportunity to learn and grow from the prestigious institute from anywhere in India. January 2025 marked a significant milestone as the students prepared for their first-term exams. These exams were conducted across 20 centres nationwide, ensuring accessibility for our diverse student base. Each centre accommodated anywhere between 7 to 200 students, making it a well-organized and seamless experience. Over the course of two days, students appeared for six exams, with three exams scheduled per day. The assessments were a mix of multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and subjective answers, designed to test both conceptual understanding and practical application of knowledge. The BBA-DBE team left no stone unturned to ensure a smooth examination process. The entire team travelled to each centre, conducting meticulous checks on facilities, from system readiness to hygiene standards. A heartwarming highlight was the team’s interaction with students and their parents’ post-exams. These conversations offered a wonderful opportunity to hear firsthand feedback, understand student experiences, and gather insights for future improvements. A group of men standing together outside Description automatically generated We are immensely proud of our learners for successfully completing their first-term exams. Their resilience and dedication have been truly inspiring. With the second term now underway, we wish all our students continued success and enriching learning experiences in the months ahead.

title: AI for Managers Batch 2 Successfully Completed
text: AI for Managers Batch 2 Successfully Completed × They Did It! Batch 2 of AI for Managers Successfully Crosses the Finish Line What a journey it has been! 125+ professionals took on the challenge of balancing work, life, and an intense 16-month learning experience—and guess what? They made it! The Certificate Programme in AI for Managers is one of our most sought-after courses, helping managers (both new and experienced) master AI-driven decision-making. And this month, Batch 2 officially became AI-certified professionals! Their dedication, perseverance, and hunger to learn have been nothing short of inspiring. So, if you’re wondering whether you can upskill while managing everything else in life—these incredible learners just proved that yes, you absolutely can! A Night to Remember: The Valedictory Ceremony We couldn’t let this achievement go by without a celebration! On February 15, 2025 , we came together for a valedictory ceremony that was filled with pride, joy, and a whole lot of high-fives! The highlight? Mr. Milesh J, Vice President of SAP Labs Pvt Ltd , joined us as the chief guest. But here’s what made it extra special—Milesh isn’t just any industry leader; he’s an alumnus of Batch 1 of this very program! He shared how AI knowledge helped him grow in his career, and honestly, his story is proof that investing in yourself always pays off. We were also honoured to have Professor Rishikesha Krishnan (Director, IIM Bangalore), Professor Dinesh Kumar (Program Director, IIMB), and Professor Vandana Singhvi Patel (Academic Director, IIMBx) with us. They cheered on the learners and applauded their hard work. A 95% Success Rate—Now That’s Something to Celebrate! Here’s a stat that speaks volumes— 95% of our learners completed the program! That’s huge! Many of them traveled from all over India just to be part of this special evening, making the celebration even more meaningful. And, of course, we had to recognize those who went the extra mile! The top performers across different courses, along with the three overall toppers of the program, were awarded for their outstanding achievements. But beyond the numbers, the real win was seeing the joy, pride, and sense of accomplishment on everyone’s faces. Watching them celebrate with their families, friends, and peers was a reminder of why we do what we do. What’s Next? The Future Looks Bright! To all our certified professionals— you did it! And this is just the beginning. You are now part of the IIMBx family and the prestigious IIMB affiliated alumni network . With your new AI expertise, we know you’re going to lead, innovate, and create real impact in your industries. Whatever comes next, we’re cheering you on every step of the way! So here’s to new beginnings, bold decisions, and a future powered by AI!

title: PCHM Batch 3: From Online Learning to Campus Life
text: PCHM Batch 3: From Online Learning to Campus Life × Campus Chronicles: PCHM Batch 3’s Journey from Screen to Scene! The Professional Certificate in Hospital Management (PCHM) is a thoughtfully designed online program, aimed at equipping healthcare professionals with essential leadership competencies. It covers areas like managing people, fostering innovation, organization design, and strategic development. The program also delves into operations, marketing, finance, economics, and the regulatory framework of healthcare in India. The third batch of PCHM kicked off in July 2024, and our learners have been thoroughly enjoying the online sessions. On January 10, 2025 , we welcomed them to an in-campus session at IIMB, bringing together a diverse group of learners from across India and even some from abroad. 110 learners in Batch 3 , more than 50% of the batch came in person to the session to experience a day in the life of an IIMB student on campus. The full day was packed with insightful activities and interactive discussions. The day began with Prof. Vasanthi Srinivasan’s energetic session on Future Ready Competencies . She guided learners to discover their potential and focus on growth within large hospital organizations. A reflective assignment was handed out to assist in their career development over the next 24 months, with the key takeaway being personal and professional growth. After the networking high tea, Prof. Allen led a session on Transforming Patient Care with Effective Communication . This session emphasized the importance of doctor-patient communication, covered legal nuances like the Consumer Protection Act and Advanced Medical Directives (living wills) , and sparked some passionate exchange of ideas and experiences. Lunch was another chance for our learners to bond over shared experiences and insights from the course. There was no sign of any of the usual post lunch dip in activity levels as Prof. Pavan Soni kept everyone engaged with his workshop on Design Thinking for Patient Centricity . The session was dynamic, with learners brainstorming over 200 ideas without any digital tools—quite a feat in today’s tech-driven world! They also created detailed mind maps of the design thinking process. The day concluded with the most eagerly anticipated campus tour . Learners were thrilled to explore the lush green IIMB campus, visit the spots where the movie 3 Idiots was shot and even indulged in some souvenir shopping at the IIMB store. It was a day filled with learning, interaction, and excitement. Seeing our learners happy and motivated reinforces our commitment to creating meaningful courses for the future. Happy Learners, Happy Us. Kudos to the entire IIMBx team!

सामान्‍य भारतीय प्रबंध संस्‍थान बेंगलूर (भाप्रसंबें) जो एशिया में अग्रणी प्रबंध स्‍नातक विद्यालय है, में 100 से अधिक पूर्णकालिक संकाय, विभिन्‍न कार्यक्रमों में 1200 से अधिक छात्र तथा एक महत्‍वपूर्ण कार्यपालक शिक्षा गतिविधि है। हम सभी स्‍तरों पर संकाय के पदों के लिए आवेदन आमंत्रित करते हैं। सहायक प्रोफेसर के स्‍तर पर उम्‍मीदवारों में उच्‍च कोटि का अनुसंधान करने की क्षमता होनी चाहिए तथा पीएचडी कार्यक्रम पूर्ण हो गया हो या अंतिम चरण पर होना चाहिए। सह प्रोफेसर के पास अनुसंधान एवं शिक्षण का निष्पादन रिकार्ड होना चाहिए। प्रोफेसरों से अतिरिक्‍त रूप में संस्‍थान में शैक्षिक नेतृत्‍व प्रदान करने की अपेक्षा होती है।  उम्‍मीदवारों से संस्‍थान के स्‍नातकोत्‍तर (एमबीए), वाचस्पति और कार्यपालक कार्यक्रमों में योगदान देने की अपेक्षा होगी। लेखांकन, संप्रेषण, अर्थशास्‍त्र, वित्‍त, मानव संसाधन, सूचना प्रणाली, नवाचार एवं उद्यमवृत्ति, विपणन, परिचालन प्रबंध, परिचालन अनुसंधान, संगठनात्‍मक व्‍यवहार, सार्वजनिक नीति, सांख्यिकी तथा कार्यनीति सहित प्रबंध एवं सार्वजनिक नीति के सभी क्षेत्रों में उम्‍मीदवारों से आवेदन आमंत्रित किए जाते हैं। इच्‍छुक उम्‍मीदवार dean.faculty[at]iimb[dot]ac[dot]in (संकायाध्यक्ष, संकाय, भाप्रसं बेंगलूर) को अपना आत्मवृत्त , संदर्भों की सूची तथा हाल के अनुसंधान के परिणामों के नमूने भेज सकते हैं। संस्‍थान के बारे में सूचना www.iimb.ac.in . पर उपलब्‍ध है। संयुक्‍त संकाय नियुक्ति हम भाप्रसं बेंगलूर तथा किसी अन्‍य अग्रणी व्‍यवसाय विद्यालय के बीच संयुक्‍त नियुक्तियों के लिए आवेदनों का स्‍वागत करते हैं। ऐसी संयुक्‍त नियुक्तियों पर संकाय से भाप्रसंबें में सामान्‍यतया हर साल लगभग 12 सप्‍ताह का कम से कम एक सत्र बिताने और पाठ्यक्रम पढ़ाने की अपेक्षा होगी। हम उम्‍मीद करते हैं कि यह भाप्रसंबें के संकाय, वाचस्पति छात्रों तथा संयुक्‍त नियुक्ति पर संकाय के बीच सतत् अनुसंधान सहयोग स्‍थापित करने का अवसर प्रदान करेगा। आवेदन संकायाध्यक्ष संकाय, भारतीय प्रबंध संस्‍थान बेंगलूर, बन्‍नेरघट्टा रोड, बेंगलूर - 560076, भारत को भेजे जा सकते हैं। ईमेल : dean.faculty[at]iimb[dot]ac[dot]in विशिष्‍ट अभ्यागत संकाय हम विशिष्‍ट अभ्यागत संकाय के पदों के लिए आवेदनों का स्‍वागत करते हैं।  उत्‍कृष्‍ट विद्वानों के लिए हमारे पास हर साल सीमित संख्‍या में ऐसे पद होते हैं। संकाय से सामान्‍यतया भाप्रसंबें में एक या अधिक सत्र बिताने और पाठ्यक्रम पढ़ाने की अपेक्षा होगी। संयुक्‍त नियुक्ति से भिन्‍न, यह दीर्घावधिक नियुक्ति नहीं है। आवेदन संकायाध्यक्ष, संकाय, भारतीय प्रबंध संस्‍थान बेंगलूर, बन्‍नेरघट्टा रोड, बेंगलूर - 560076, भारत को भेजे जा सकते हैं। ईमेल : dean.faculty[at]iimb[dot]ac[dot]in हम संस्‍थान में शिक्षण एवं अनुसंधान के सभी पदों (शैक्षणिक अंतःशिक्षु, अनुबद्ध संकाय, अभ्यागत संकाय, कार्यावधि पर संकाय) के लिए आवेदन करने हेतु ओबीसी, एससी / एसटी, पीडब्‍ल्‍यूडी उम्‍मीदवारों को प्रोत्‍साहित करते हैं। ------------------------------------------- आईआई एम बेंगलूर को अपना वृत्ति गंतव्य बनाने के दस कारण: भाप्रसंबें में जीवन: व्यवहार के प्रोफेसर संकाय पद - एनआईआरएफ आईआईएमबी वैबमेल सर्वम वैशिष्ट्य मीडिया कक्ष परिसर दौरा निबंधन एवं शर्तें गोपनीयता नीति सर्वाधिकार नीति हाइपरलिंक नीति अभिगम्यता विवरण प्रतिक्रिया सहायता खंडन इस साइट के बारे में उपयोग की संस्थान बेंगलूर (भाप्रसंबें) समग्र, रूपांतकारी एवं नवीन शिक्षा के माध्यम से नेताओं का निर्माण करने में विश्वास करता है । और पढ़िए >> भाप्रसंबें के विषय में भारतीय प्रबंधन संस्थान बैंगलोर (IIMB) एशिया में प्रबंधन का एक अग्रणी स्नातक स्कूल है। 2017 के IIM अधिनियम के तहत , IIMB एक राष्ट्रीय महत्व का संस्थान है। IIMB में 109 पूर्णकालिक संकाय सदस्य, विभिन्न डिग्री-अनुदान कार्यक्रमों में लगभग 1,200 छात्र और लगभग 5,000 वार्षिक कार्यकारी शिक्षा प्रतिभागी हैं। हमारे लोगो में संस्कृत में एक उद्घोषणा है, तेजस्वि नावधीतमस्तु (तेजस्वी नावधीतमस्तु), जिसका अनुवाद है 'हमारे अध्ययन को ज्ञानवर्धक बनाएं'। हमारा लक्ष्य व्यवसाय, सरकार और समाज के लिए प्रबंधन, नवाचार और उद्यमिता में उत्कृष्टता को बढ़ावा देने वाला एक वैश्विक, प्रसिद्ध शैक्षणिक संस्थान बनना है। भारत की उच्च प्रौद्योगिकी राजधानी में स्थित, हम सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी से लेकर उपभोक्ता उत्पाद कंपनियों तक देश के कुछ प्रमुख कॉर्पोरेट घरानों के करीब हैं, जिससे हमें व्यावहारिक अनुभव के साथ कक्षा ज्ञान को एकीकृत करने का अतिरिक्त लाभ मिलता है। हमारे लंबी अवधि के कार्यक्रमों में डॉक्टर ऑफ फिलॉसफी (पीएचडी), प्रबंधन में स्नातकोत्तर कार्यक्रम (पीजीपी), प्रबंधन में स्नातकोत्तर कार्यक्रम - बिजनेस एनालिटिक्स (पीजीपी-बीए), प्रबंधन में कार्यकारी स्नातकोत्तर कार्यक्रम (पीजीपी-बीए) शामिल हैं। प्रबंधन में कार्यकारी स्नातकोत्तर कार्यक्रम (ईपीजीपी), और एंटरप्राइज मैनेजमेंट में पोस्ट ग्रेजुएट प्रोग्राम (पीजीपीईएम)। हम भारत में प्रबंधन शिक्षा जगत की सामाजिक विविधता को बढ़ाने के उद्देश्य से एक प्रमाणपत्र कार्यक्रम के रूप में एनएस रामास्वामी प्री-डॉक्टरल (एनएसआर प्री-डॉक्टर) फ़ेलोशिप प्रदान करते हैं। हम महात्मा गांधी राष्ट्रीय फ़ेलोशिप (एमजीएनएफ) कार्यक्रम भी प्रदान करते हैं। एमजीएनएफ आईआईएम द्वारा पेश सार्वजनिक नीति और प्रबंधन में एक प्रमाणपत्र कार्यक्रम है। इसे भारत सरकार के कौशल विकास और उद्यमिता मंत्रालय (एमएसडीई) की पहल पर डिजाइन किया गया है और राज्य कौशल विकास मिशन (एसएसडीएम) के सहयोग से कार्यान्वित किया गया है। 11 अनुशासनात्मक क्षेत्रों के साथ, हमारे पास उत्कृष्टता के दस केंद्र हैं जो पाठ्यक्रम प्रदान करते हैं और उद्योग के विभिन्न क्षेत्रों के सामने आने वाले दिलचस्प सवालों पर शोध करते हैं। महिला उद्यमिता के लिए गोल्डमैन सैक्स और कोटक बैंक के साथ, गैर-लाभकारी संस्थाओं के उद्भव के लिए माइकल और सुसान डेल फाउंडेशन के साथ, और नए उद्यमों को बढ़ाने के लिए नीति आयोग के साथ हमारी प्रमुख साझेदारियां और सहयोग हैं। हम प्रौद्योगिकी-सक्षम शिक्षा का उपयोग करके गहरा सामाजिक प्रभाव डालने के लिए प्रतिबद्ध हैं। इस दिशा में, हम व्यापक ओपन ऑनलाइन पाठ्यक्रम (एमओओसी) प्रदान करते हैं। हम ईडीएक्स प्लेटफॉर्म पर एमओओसी की पेशकश करने वाले भारत के पहले प्रबंधन स्कूल हैं। हम भारत सरकार के ऑनलाइन शिक्षा मंच SWAYAM के लिए प्रबंधन शिक्षा के लिए समन्वय संस्थान भी हैं। हमने आईआईएमबी के लिए निर्धारित दृष्टिकोण को पूरा करने के लिए कई कदम उठाए हैं। इनमें उच्च गुणवत्ता वाले संकाय को नियुक्त करना, अनुसंधान की गुणवत्ता को बढ़ाना, अंतर्राष्ट्रीयकरण पर जोर देना, अनुसंधान और परामर्श दोनों में उद्यमिता के क्षेत्र में हमारी गतिविधियों का विस्तार करना, सभी कार्यक्रमों में छात्र प्रवेश के मामले में वृद्धि करना, पूर्व छात्रों के साथ हमारी भागीदारी को गहरा करना, बुनियादी ढांचे, और प्रशासन और शासन में सुधार करना शामिल है। हमें 2016 में पांच साल की अवधि के लिए EFMD क्वालिटी इम्प्रूवमेंट सिस्टम (EQUIS) द्वारा मान्यता प्राप्त थी। EQUIS यूरोपियन फाउंडेशन फॉर मैनेजमेंट डेवलपमेंट (EFMD) द्वारा संचालित एक वैश्विक स्कूल मान्यता प्रणाली है जो प्रबंधन और व्यवसाय प्रशासन के उच्च शिक्षा संस्थानों में विशेषज्ञता रखती है। पांच साल की मान्यता, जो EQUIS द्वारा प्रदान की जाने वाली सर्वोच्च मान्यता है, इस तथ्य का प्रमाण है कि मूल्यांकन करने वाली टीम शिक्षा, अंतर्राष्ट्रीयकरण और अनुसंधान में उत्कृष्ट मानकों को प्राप्त करने के लिए किए गए प्रयासों को बनाए रखने की हमारी क्षमता के प्रति आश्वस्त थी। उत्तरी अमेरिका, दक्षिण अमेरिका, यूरोप, एशिया और ऑस्ट्रेलिया में कई साझेदार विश्वविद्यालयों के साथ हमारा एक जीवंत छात्र विनिमय कार्यक्रम है। हमारा अंतरराष्ट्रीय नेटवर्क, ग्लोबल नेटवर्क फॉर एडवांस्ड मैनेजमेंट (जीएनएएम) के साथ गहरा जुड़ाव है, जिसमें दुनिया भर के 32 प्रतिष्ठित बिजनेस स्कूल शामिल हैं। हम बन्नेरघट्टा रोड परिसर से लगभग 27 किमी दूर जिगनी में अपना दूसरा परिसर विकसित कर रहे हैं। हम विस्तार और विकास के एक रोमांचक पथ पर हैं, और इस यात्रा में हमारे साथ जुड़ने के लिए हम आपका स्वागत करते हैं। भाप्रसंबें होम के विषय में भाप्रसंबें के विषय में आदर्श वाक्य विज़न मिशन मूल्य मार्गदर्शी सिद्धांत प्रेरणा, उत्कृष्टता, उपलब्धि वास्तुशिल्प प्रत्यायन एवं रैंकिंग मंडल अध्यक्ष द्वारा संदेश निदेशक का संदेश आईआईएमबी अधिनियम एवं नियम संगठनात्मक संरचना अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सलाहकार समिति इतिहास घटनाक्रम हमारी यात्रा... भाप्रसंबें की इतिहास परियोजना सहयोग उन्नत प्रबंध हेतु वैश्विक नेटवर्क जीएनएएम के माध्यम से साझेदार छात्र विनिमय सहयोग अनुसंधान और शिक्षा साझेदारी भाप्रसंबें में जीवन होम परिसर अध्ययन परिवेश आवास प्रेरणा स्रोत बेंगलूर अध्ययन परिवेश आवास समान अवसर आंतरिक समिति समिति सदस्य विशाखा दिशा-निर्देश अधिनियम कार्यस्थल के उपाय भाप्रसंबें को यौन उत्पीड़न मुक्त परिसर बनाने हेतु नीति भाप्रसंबें को यौन उत्पीड़न मुक्त परिसर बनाने के लिए नीति भाप्रसंबें में रैगिंग-विरोधी नीति सूचना प्रदाता नीति कन्नड़ हिंदी अंग्रेज़ी पुस्तकालय कार्यक्रम @ आईआईएमबी
