He has taught and conducted research at leading international institutions such as the University of St. Gallen, HEC Paris, Bocconi University, and the University of Gothenburg. At IIM Bangalore, he has held several senior roles including Dean – Administration and Chair – Executive Post Graduate Programme. Prof. Shainesh has advised major organizations across sectors— ranging from Indian Oil and Tata Motors to Sanofi and the Ministry of Tourism—and is the Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of Indian Business Research. His publications, award winning case studies, and books on CRM and social media marketing have earned him widespread recognition, including the CMO Asia “Best Professor in Marketing” Award. G Ajay Row Founder & Chairman, Customer Capital G. Ajay Row is an entrepreneur and executive with nearly 40 years in data-driven marketing, loyalty, analytics and CRM across a number of industries. He launched one of the first loyalty and data-driven marketing programs globally in the ‘80s for ITC. Since implemented programs across 65+ countries. He has built several companies, won numerous awards, and delivered a number of globally recognized case studies in loyalty and CRM. He graduated in Economics and Statistics from St. Xavier’s College, Bombay and Marketing and Systems from IIM Calcutta. Scores of Loyalty and CRM programs delivered include: Taj Inner Circle (consistent Freddie award winner, rated the best hospitality loyalty program globally) and five other CRM programs for the Taj Group, Landmark’s Shukran (one of the largest retail loyalty programs globally), Axis Bank eDGE (one of the world’s first and largest pan-bank programs), Welcome Award (for ITC Hotels, first loyalty program outside the US), Shoppers Stop’s First Citizen (considered the best retail program, original launch and recent relaunch), Gujarat Ambuja Cement (still the only loyalty program I know of for illiterates), Citibank, Standard Chartered Bank 360o, Providian, HSBC (Household), Citizens, American Express, Ford, Honda, Maruti, Mercedes, IBM, Microsoft, Eureka Forbes, Mauritius Tourism, the list goes on. Whether you’re leading a business unit, managing projects, or heading marketing and operations – every decision impacts the bottom line. The Finance for Non-Finance Executives (FNFE) programme at IIM Bangalore is crafted for professionals from non-financial backgrounds who want to confidently navigate financial statements, make informed decisions, and drive business growth. This is not just a finance course – it’s a strategic business enabler. Programme Objectives Equip non-finance managers with a strong foundation in key financial concepts and terminology. Enable participants to read, interpret, and analyse financial statements with confidence. Enhance decision-making capabilities by understanding the financial impact of business activities. Develop the ability to evaluate investment opportunities, budgeting plans, and cost structures. Introduce key aspects of commercial law, direct and indirect taxation relevant to business. Build cross-functional collaboration by improving communication with finance teams and stakeholders. Foster strategic thinking by linking financial metrics to business performance and value creation. Prepare participants to take on larger leadership roles with greater financial responsibility. Ideal For Entrepreneurs and Consultants with mid-to-senior professionals across industries. Also suitable for professionals in leadership role without formal finance training Certificate & Alumni Status A certificate of completion will be awarded by IIMB to participants upon successful completion of the programme and satisfying programme requirements. Contact Us Mr. Emthias Asin Email: emthias.asin@iimb.ac.in Mobile #:  8951974077 Key Benefits Financial Confidence : Learn to read and interpret financial statements, profit & loss accounts, and cash flow statements with ease. Smarter Decisions : Understand the financial impact behind critical business choices to make informed decisions. Cross-Functional Power : Communicate more effectively with finance teams and key stakeholders. Strategic Influence : Gain the confidence to participate in boardroom discussions and budgeting processes. Career Advancement : Earn a certificate from IIM Bangalore and gain prestigious alumni status to elevate your professional profile. Programme Directors Professor Padmini Srinivasan Professor Padmini Srinivasan is a distinguished faculty member at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, serving as the Chairperson of the Executive Education Programmes and Chairperson of the Centre for Corporate Governance and Sustainability. A Fellow Chartered Accountant and an Associate Company Secretary, she brings a rare blend of academic excellence and industry experience to the classroom. At IIMB, she teaches core finance subjects such as Financial Reporting & Analysis and Corporate Governance to postgraduate and executive students. Professor Padmini has also designed and delivered multiple executive education programmes. Her depth of knowledge and approachable teaching style make her an invaluable mentor in this programme. Professor S. Shanker Professor S. Shanker is a highly respected management consultant and academician with over 25 years of multi-functional and cross-industry experience. With a professional background spanning leading companies such as Hindustan Unilever, Shaw Wallace, and Ecolab, he has held senior roles in marketing, supply chain, legal, and international trade. He is an Adjunct Faculty at IIM Bangalore and also teaches at IIM Shillong and IIM Udaipur. Professor Shanker is widely known for his engaging and practical approach to teaching subjects such as Commercial Law and International Trade. His sessions bring alive the legal and commercial aspects of finance. And the only way to do great work is to love what you do. If you haven’t found it yet, keep looking. Don’t settle. As with all matters of the heart, you’ll know when you find it. And, like any great relationship, it just gets better and better as the years roll on.” – Steve Jobs The fast pace of change that is driving social, political, and business context in today’s India has already created an unprecedented variety of psychological impact on individuals. This impact coupled with relentless globalization of economy, over last few years has led to a progressive disintegration between employee(s) and organization(s) as against a backdrop of long tenured and sustained symbiotic relationship that was the hallmark of Indian industries across the country. With frequent reorganizing, rightsizing, delayering, teaming, flattening the pyramid, outsourcing and M&A’s taking place more regularly on one hand, and steady increase in Gen Y Population with easy access to information on the other have significantly impacted careers and career development processes in organizations. Career has assumed a new meaning among the mid-career professionals in recent years. The expectations of these careerists from organizations have changed significantly and thus the ways to career success have also changed significantly. This has created a big challenge to mid- career professionals in terms of inventing new career strategies for their success. The more challenging, complex, and contrasting the needs of professionals from organizations are becoming, the more pressure is being built in the internal organizational system to enable business leaders and HR professionals to think out of box, to change the traditional rule of engagement that are based on external perspective and build innovative career management system that has roots more on internal career perspective. Under this backdrop, there is a fundamental need for mid-career professionals to become aware of career strategies that can fulfil their career aspirations for short as well as long term. Consequently, these career strategies contribute to ensuring that the pluralistic career orientations of mid-career professionals are met and ensure their personal and professional growth. Programme Objective This three-day program is aimed at enabling participants to: • Understand the impact of societal culture on organizational career management (OCM) system and current trends in career management. • Understand driver(s) for individual career orientation and its impact on career progression and career satisfaction and test the same for self. • Understand the significance of basic tenets of a career strategy that are required to build a successful career strategy. • Become aware of socio-cultural stimuli that are significantly impacting their individual career choice. • Learn about how to build appropriate competencies keeping in mind both their life and career stages. Contact Us Preethi S Mobile: (+91) 89519 74073 Email: preethi.s@iimb.ac.in Eligibility This program is meant for mid-career professionals who are looking for more clarity and direction to build a Career strategy for ensuring success from all domains including Indian Conglomerate, MNCs and Startups as well as entrepreneurs and independent consultants. This program will be very useful for professionals who are on sabbatical/career break and awaiting their next career move. Pedagogy • Use of psychometric instruments to examine one’s strengths and weaknesses. • Individual and team-based work supported by appropriate career coaching, video clippings and case studies. • Interactive methods of learning. Participant Benefits In current times, the onus of career development and growth is slowly but definitely shifting from organization to the individuals. Hence every careerist in order to achieve their career fulfillment need to be aware of his / her own strength, which stage of life stage he/she is in, which career stage he/she is passing through and build a career strategy for success and growth. Building a balance between career achievement and career fulfilment requires clarity and understanding of how to navigate through for future in mid-way in their careers. This three-day program is meant especially for the mid-career professionals to become aware of – a) Where they are? b) Where their strength lies? c) How to they build a career strategy to achieve success and growth in future? Some of the exclusive benefits of attending this programme are listed below – Receive Executive Education eNewsletters Participate in EEP webinars on various topics Invitation to curated events and programmes by the EEP office Invitation to share articles to the EEP blog (subject to a shortlisting process) Programme Directors Apurva Sanaria has more than 20 years of rich experience across corporate, consulting, and academics including ICICI Group, Future Group, Kantar Group, and T.V. Rao Learning Systems (TVRLS). He completed PhD in Organizational Behaviour from XLRI-Jamshedpur. He is accredited for FIRO-B (psychometric assessment), Competency Mapping, Assessment & Development Centers (ADCs), and Transactional Analysis (TA). He has contributed to enhancing the effectiveness of various organizations by providing consulting services including Leadership Development, Career & Succession Planning, Competency Mapping, Assessment & Development Centers (ADCs), and Designing Performance Management Systems (PMS). He has also conducted corporate trainings for numerous organizations. He has published papers in top journals (including FT50 journals). His research papers have been selected for presentation at international conferences in India, China,and USA. Dr. Pallab Bandyopadhyay is a Leadership Architect, Career Coach, Change and Transition Specialist. A doctoral fellow in HRD from XLRI, Jamshedpur, and trained at various human process and organization development interventions at NTL, USA, he is also certified in Hogan and Thomas personality profile assessments. Dr. Pallab has more than three decades of successful professional experience in managing entire gamut of Human Resources Management with proven expertise in managing multicultural globally distributed knowledge professionals as head of HR functions at Country/Regional/ Global levels at Citrix Systems, Dell services, Perot systems, Cambridge Solutions, Sasken Communication Technologies, Ashok Leyland Information Technology and National Dairy Development Board (NDDB). In his role as a strategic HR leader, he has been responsible for providing HR leadership to achieve business growth through people in multi-cultural and multi-locational complex and dynamic work environment in USA, Europe, India, and APAC region. Dr Pallab helps his client organizations to bring an alignment of people strategies with the business goals through a rare combination of practice and concepts. He is currently engaged in providing HR consulting to many large Indian and MNCs and start-ups around Leadership Development, New-Manager Development, Executive Coaching, Organization Development, Long-term competency development for HR professionals, M&A, HR Restructuring, Organization Talent Management, Organization Career Management, Strategic Change, Organization Design and Alignment. He has worked with diverse set of people and business leaders from organization like ABB, Astra Zeneca, Aquarelle, Asian Institute of Technology (AIT) Bangkok ,Bank Of India (BOI), Believe Music, CareerNet, CGI, Cyient, Cadilla Pharmaceuticals, Cambridge Silicon Radio (CSR), Continental, DCM-Sriram, Deloitte, Dr Reddy’s Laboratory (DRL), Emami Group, Flytxt, Honeywell Technology Solutions (HTS), KPMG, L&T, Mercedes Benz, Manhattan Associates, Merck, Novartis, PI Industries, Piramal Group Rasi Group, RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group, SanDisk, Sabre, Siemens Health Care, State Bank of India (SBI), Sears, Schneider Electric, Sun Guard, Symbiosis Institute of Management Science (SIMS), The Hindu, The Manipal Group, Unisys, Zensar Technologies, and Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Indore. He has vast expertise in change and transition management having lead people related strategic interventions in twenty- five M&A deals across the globe. Dr Pallab was on the national board of NHRDN and also one of the past-Presidents of NHRD Bangalore chapter and a member at the National HR and IR/ER committee of CII. He has been the member of the national level design team of NHRDN that created the HR competency model (HRSCAPE) which is being used to assess competencies of HR professionals across the country. He has published several papers in leading HR journals and the Managing Editor for NHRDN Journal which is currently published by SAGE. He is also a visiting faculty at XLRI, Jamshedpur, IIM Lucknow, Indore, and Kozhikode in the area of HRM/OB. Dr Pallab is a research guide for PhD students under the Faculty of Management Symbiosis University, a member of the academic advisory board at Christ University Institute of Management. Dr Pallab is also a certified executive coach and spends considerable time in coaching and mentoring both senior business and technology leaders as well as HR professionals across the country. He has been a recipient of Super Achievers Award for two times and HR Leadership Award once for his outstanding achievements in the field of HR. He also sits in the advisory board of two vibrant startups at Bangalore. He is also featured as one of the six exemplary HR leaders who have humanized workplaces in India with their courage, candor and consistent calling to ethical services in the book Being People. The programme would also cover Operational issues in Digital Supply Chain and Business Analytics. Programme Overview The Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0) is unfolding the age of digitalization by eliminating traditional industrial practices in Operations and Supply Chain Management. Large-scale Machine-to-Machine (M2M) communication and Internet of Things (IoT) are integrated for automation escalation, seamless communication, and production to pinpoint issues without the need for human intervention. The programme will bring together participants from diverse backgrounds, skills, and experience, thereby enabling peer learning. The participants will involve themselves actively in case studies, and simulation games. They benefit immensely through continuous learning and networking with peers from different backgrounds, during and after the programme. Key Benefits Identifying issues that may create value in supply chains through digitization and data analytics. Understanding of the applications of business analytics for enhancing productivity and achieving cost- efficiency. Understanding the applications of data analytics techniques in demand and supply management. Leveraging data for Digital Transformation. Understanding the implications of various Digital Technologies on the operational aspects in Supply Chains. Programme Directors Prof. Tarun Jain is a Professor in the Production and Operations Management Area at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore. His research interests include strategic sourcing, operational issues in cloud computing, management of digital technologies, smart city operations, urban mobility, and pricing issues in service supply chains. (Email: tarun.jain@iimb.ac.in) Prof. Shubhabrata Das is a Professor in Decision Sciences at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore. He has held visiting faculty positions at various institutes/ universities of international repute, including ESSEC Business School, Indian Statistical Institute Calcutta, University of Nebraska, and University of Montana. (Email: shubho@iimb.ac.in) Target Audience Mid-Senior career professionals with minimum of 3 years’ experience Practitioners and aspirants in Digital Manufacturing, Project Management, Revenue Management, Managing Digital Platforms, E-commerce Category Management, Retailing, Services, and Logistics Sectors. production planning and scheduling Probability models for operations and supply chain management Sampling and estimation Process and capacity analysis Managing capacity under uncertainties Testimonials “ As a technology practitioner myself, I was overwhelmed with the course. I learnt strategies and concepts along with the importance of adopting technology, which drives SCM and Operations, at right time. The entire learning experience became exciting with 50% of the modules framed as Gamification. I strongly recommend this course for any SCM and Operation professional in their early stages of digital adoption. Prem Anand Senior Manager, Market Solutions - Denso International India Pvt Ltd “ I came to know about this programme from IIMB while I was planning to upskill. My learning journey has been very enriching. While I aced all my exams, I was truly humbled with professional experience of my peers. It was an incredible experience as we learned from each other during classroom, assignments, and project submission. I have experimented with some of the tools learned during the programme and have automated my Weekly Business Reports as well as Daily Building Health reports. It has helped me to analyse data much efficiently as well as have reduced time spent by my team to collect data (which was earlier done manually). Further, based on stocking cost, we are in process of moving all my engineering stores inventory to automated tools with defined ‘Reorder points’ taking into account variability. As I reflect on my 6 months learning programme, I’m glad that I enrolled for the programme and met esteemed IIMB faculty who have sharpened my thought process, my analytical skills, and my reasoning. Shalabh Vijay Sector Head , Projects - Amazon Seller Services Pvt Ltd “ As I enrolled for this programme, I had high expectations which have been met and have actually surpassed in every aspect. From the comprehensive curriculum to the outstanding faculty and invaluable networking opportunities, this program has truly been a game-changer for me. The program’s curriculum was meticulously designed to provide a holistic understanding of digital operations and supply chain management. The coursework covered a wide range of topics, including digital transformation, logistics, procurement, inventory management and demand forecasting, among others. The blend of theoretical concepts, case studies and practical applications ensured that we developed a deep understanding of the subject matter and acquired the necessary skills to excel in the field. What truly sets this program apart is the calibre of the faculty members at IIMB. Their ability to connect theory with real-world examples and challenges was truly commendable. They not only imparted knowledge but also encouraged critical thinking and fostered a collaborative learning environment. Another aspect that made the program exceptional was the opportunity to interact and network with professionals from diverse backgrounds. The resources and learning materials provided were up-to-date and easily accessible, which greatly enhanced the learning journey. The programme has equipped me with the necessary knowledge, skills and confidence to navigate the complex and rapidly evolving landscape of the industry. The insights gained from this program have already proven invaluable in my professional endeavours, enabling me to make data driven decisions, optimize processes ,and drive efficiencies within my organization. Harshit Srivastava Business Analyst - Koch Industries (Koch Global Services India) “ Having been into Industry from 27+ years and leading Supply Chain function from 13+ years, the changing global business environment with focus on sustainability and adoption of digital technologies are throwing continuous challenges. In order to keep our Supply Chain competitive, it needed to be modern and agile, and as a leader of this process one need to be well versed with changes happening in the surroundings, for that purpose I was looking for a suitable course, and that is when I came across this certification. The course is very focussed in its approach and covers most of the things needed and I must say it exceeded all my expectations. The course content was comprehensive and futuristic, covering a wide range of cutting-edge technologies like AI / ML / IOT / Edge AI concepts and its application in SCM, Business Analytics with use of Advance Excel Analytics, Supply and Demand Concepts and it’s applications, Pricing and Revenue Management, Strategy and other useful concepts. Faculty is highly knowledgeable and experienced, providing engaging lectures and practical hands-on exercises with case studies and Simulation games. IIMB Supply Chain Management Center was very helpful in providing Engaging Projects from Industry, I was fortunate to get a Sustainability Project with Schneider Electric which was successfully completed under the guidance from faculty. Moreover, the course offered a perfect balance between theoretical concepts and real-world applications, enabling me to gain valuable skills applicable to today’s tech-driven world I highly recommend this course to anyone seeking to master the Supply chain skills and wanted to stay ahead in the rapidly evolving world of modern technologies. Vikas Tyagi Director, Supply Chain Operations - SMPL Top-notch faculty, contemporary content, a great learning environment, and application orientation make the IIMB Exec Ed programmes world-class. This programme will help in transforming bold creative ideas into blockbuster products and services, lead and inspire entertainment business organizational change taking into account technological advancements in the entertainment business and drive operational excellence, growth and profitability. The programme will also place a strong emphasis on the Creator Economy — the rapidly growing ecosystem of independent content creators, influencers, streamers, podcasters, and digital entrepreneurs who are leveraging platforms such as YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Twitch, and other emerging channels to build audiences, monetize content, and launch brands. EBMP will explore how creators can professionalize their operations, develop sustainable business models, protect intellectual property, and collaborate with traditional entertainment firms. Special focus will be placed on helping participants understand platform algorithms, community engagement, multiplatform monetization strategies, and brand partnerships that drive long-term growth. Programme Objective The programme aims to help you to expand your vision for managing and sustaining the growth of your entertainment business. Develop  organizational, financial and marketing strategies for driving business growth. Transform creative concepts to successfully implemented projects. Drive operational excellence and sustain the growth of the content and the growth of the business in multiple arenas of entertainment. Create entertainment value and appropriate Business value from your ventures. Programme Content Programme Director Prof. S. Raghunath , is  Professor of Strategy. He teaches the Strategic Management In Media & Entertainment course at IIM Bangalore. He offers the General Management Programme for Film Producers, Directors, Studio Owners, Film Distributors & Exhibitors and General Managers of Media & Entertainment companies based on his field research and case studies for the past ten years.     He was the Chairperson for the Centre for Corporate Governance and Citizenship. He is the Chairman of the South Asia Board of the Academy of International Business. He specializes in Strategic Alliances and Strategic Leadership. He was also the Programme Director for International Master’s Programme for Practicing Managers. Dr. Raghunath is on the board of directors of several hi-tech companies. He is a Registered Consultant with the Office of Project Services, UNDP, and New York. He has published several papers, case studies and book chapter and has been quoted in publications such as Economic Times, Business Line and the Computer Today. He was a Visiting Scholar at the Graduate School of Business, Stanford University where he engaged in research in strategy making in IT companies. He was also a Visiting Professor at the University of Buckingham, UK; RMIT School of Business, Melbourne, Australia, HEC, Paris and INSEAD, France. Prof. Anil B Suraj , is Associate Professor of Practice Centre for Public Policy and Chairperson, Post Graduate Programme in Public Policy and Management. He is a member of the advisory council of the Centre For Corporate Governance and Citizenship at IIMB and is also the Chairperson, Office of Diversity & Inclusion. He delivers core courses on – Public Administration and Law for the Doctoral students, and Business Law for the MBA Programme, and for the Executive Management Programmes. Suraj has jointly coordinated the Phase-IV Mid-Career Training Programme in 2008, 2009 and 2010 for the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) Officers, and regularly delivers technical sessions to Midcareer programmes of various All India Services on “Judicial Review of Policy making”, “Fiduciary levels of Accountability in Governance”; “Public Contracts and Projects”; “WTO & TRIPs”; and “Intellectual Property Rights & Data Protection”. Suraj has also addressed Senior Bureaucrats of – South Korea, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Sri Lanka, and from more than 45 countries Africa. Many of these technical sessions have been at the invite of the National Centre for Good Governance, Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration, Mussoorie, Uttarakhand, India. Prior to joining IIM Bangalore in March 2007, Suraj was a Research Fellow at the National Judicial Academy, India, wherein he coordinated training courses for senior District Judges and High Court Justices on various topics, including – Economic Analysis of Law and Adjudication of Economic Laws. At the Academy, Suraj was involved in coordinating the first ever initiative of a course module and a training programme on Court Management and Judicial Administration in India. Suraj has also been a Member of the first Working Group of the Planning Commission for Union Ministry of Law and Justice for the 12th Five Year Plan (2012-2017). Mr. Rajiv Menon is an Indian filmmaker who has worked as a director and cinematographer in several Indian regional films. After making his breakthrough as a film cinematographer with Mani Ratnam’s drama Bombay (1994), Menon has continued to collaborate with Ratnam on other projects including Guru (2007) & Kadal (2013). He has also directed 2 critically acclaimed Tamil films, Minsara Kanavu (1997) and Kandukondain Kandukondain (2000), winning a Filmfare Award for the latter. After a sabbatical, Menon returned to directing with Sarvam Thaala Mayam. Away from films, Menon is a leading Indian advertising director, and runs Rajiv Menon Productions and Mindscreen Film Institute, which supplies equipment for documentaries, advertising films and cinemas. Contact Us Ms. Mohsina Jabeen Mobile No. +91-7899991516 Email: mohsina.eep@iimb.ac.in Award of Certificate A part time programme certificate of completion will be awarded by IIMB to participants upon successful completion of the programme and satisfying programme requirements. IIMB EEP Alumni Membership The participants become IIMB EEP alumni on successful completion of the programme and thereby gain access to the alumni network across various industry sectors. Programme & Payment Schedule Programme Schedule: *Hybrid – Participants who are in Bangalore or can travel to Bangalore are welcome to attend the classes on our campus. Alternatively, they have the option to attend these classes live online via Zoom. Payment Schedule: Who Should Apply? This programme is designed for those who currently own an entertainment business or manage an entertainment business as well as for those who plan to start an entertainment business or plan to join the media and entertainment industry as a manager. Also for those who have completed their education specializing. Certificate Sample A  certificate of participation will be awarded by IIMB to participants upon successful completion of the programme. You are required to upload your Resume and Graduation Certificate in the online application portal. For any queries related to the programme, please contact Mr. Shashidhara C S on Phone no. +91-7899991576 or Email ID at shashidhara.cs@iimb.ac.in Aamir Khan on the programme Boman Irani on the programme Video Testimonials Testimonials “ IIM Bangalore’s General Management Programme on Media and Entertainment Business is Prof. Raghunath and Mr Rajiv Menon’s brainchild. Prof Raghunath is an institution in himself and along with Mr Rajiv Menon, has curated a course which covers all businesses in the media industry – how it runs and how it can be revived. Through this programme, we got an array framework as to how to solve media business problems. Prof. Raghunath brought Industry veterans like Rajiv Menon and Dilip Mehta – along with many executives who are running television, advertising, music and film business. As I was already engaged in several projects during the course of this programme, I was able to manage my time while using and implementing the learnings from this course. Ganesh Pareek (GEM 1) Executive Producer, Partner & Design Thinking Head - First December Films “ IIM Bangalore’s General Management Programme on Media and Entertainment Business has been a game-changer. The program gave me a deep understanding of the industry and equipped me with the skills to lead and manage effectively. The opportunity to network with industry professionals has been invaluable. Overall, I highly recommend this program to anyone looking to excel in the media and entertainment field. Abhinav Kamal (GEM 1) Film Director, Company Director - Ten Motion Arts Pvt Ltd “ The programme is thoughtfully structured and gives a balanced learning of both creative and business side of the entertainment world. Perfect programme for working professionals who would like to switch to media & entertainment domain and create value in this high growth sector which has a deficit of domain specific educated professionals. Vibhore Mayank (GEM 1) CEO - Knocksense “ General Management in Media and Entertainment course offered by IIM Bangalore is a holistic program which covers both the business and creative aspects of entertainment business. The course which covers Strategy, Operations, Marketing, Finance and Legal aspects of the business, has participants with vast industry experience and exposure and due to this the class interactions have been enriching. We were exposed to the basics of creative domains such as lighting, art direction, and production as well which was possible because of industry speakers/lecturers. Om Prakash Pal (GEM 1) Associate Director - Cognizant Technology Solutions “ This was an outstanding learning experience! The programme was well-structured, engaging, and comprehensive. One of the things I appreciated the most about the course was the practical approach it took while teaching entertainment and media management. The instructors didn’t just cover theoretical concepts but also gave real-life examples and case studies to help us understand how these concepts apply in the real world. This made the course incredibly relevant and useful. I also enjoyed the variety of topics covered in the course. From marketing and promotion to contract negotiation and intellectual property law, the course covered a broad range of topics that are essential for anyone interested in a career in entertainment and media management. Overall, I would highly recommend this course to anyone interested in entertainment and media management. It was an excellent learning experience for working professionals. Sreedhar Sundarrajan G (GEM 1) Versioning Producer - Audio & Video - Hogarth Worldwide “ This course has provided an excellent learning experience in entertainment and media. We were able to interact with leaders in the entertainment industry and gain a lot of insights and perspective which cannot be found in textbooks alone. The assignments that we completed during the course were instrumental in building my confidence and skills. The course structure was designed to help us understand the different aspects of the industry and identify where I would best fit in. I am excited and eager to implement my newfound knowledge in the world of entertainment. Manasa Venkat (GEM 1) Assistant Director - Studio Shakti “ The Programme is a balanced certification for working professionals who are interested in building a career in the high growth Media and Entertainment Industry as it combines the art of creating content and the business of promoting content. I greatly benefitted with valuable insights into the end-to-end process of the media and entertainment business. I would like to extend my heartfelt gratitude to Prof. S. Raghunath, Mr Rajiv Menon and all the guest faculties for sharing their knowledge and experience. Preeti Sondur (GEM 1) Founder and Artistic Director - Natarang School of Fance “ I come from a creative background and even though I have very strong roots in this sector, I wanted something that would legitimise my skills and make me stand apart in the industry as a professional. I happened to find this programme at that transitory phase in my life right after I completed business school. Since our speakers were all seasoned industry professionals, I think it was tremendously valuable to be able to learn from the people at the very centre of it all. The sessions were delivered in form of interactive learning sessions and an active participation. It helped us tap into ourselves which helped me discover more about the way I operate. I was also able to meet some amazing peers in this short span of our learning journey and I am excited to see what we’ll come up with in the future. Simren Simha (GEM 1) Artist “ I was seeking a career transition to something more professionally fulfilling when I discovered this course. Coming from a creative background, I aimed to gain insights into the business side of the industry, and this course effectively bridged that gap. Beyond the invaluable lessons from our esteemed faculty, I deeply value the enriching peer learning experiences with our wonderful cohort. The course has unveiled new possibilities for me, notably instilling the confidence to start my own venture. I am eager to make more meaningful contributions to the Media & Entertainment industry. Viddesh Gharpure (GEM 2) Post Production Consultant “ My friend pursued a Master’s in Entertainment Industry Management at Carnegie Mellon. Seeking a similar opportunity in India, I discovered IIM-B’s long-duration program in Entertainment and Media Business. My learning journey has been incredible, pushing me out of my comfort zone and immersing me in six months of intensive learning and unlearning. I plan to start a content production house incorporating Artificial Intelligence, and I am confident that the valuable insights gained from this course will be instrumental in this endeavour. Vignesh Raghavan (GEM 2) Screenwriter, Guru Films Pvt Ltd “ This exceptional program arrived just when I was seeking opportunities to understand the business side of the film industry after spending around seven years in creative roles. Business involves assembling diverse elements in the best possible way to create a beautiful structure. This program has shaped my thought process, encouraging me to analyse situations, apply suitable frameworks, and derive effective solutions to thrive. In today’s world, there is a high demand for trained and skilled professionals in the Media & Entertainment industry. I hope this opens doors for us to collaborate with the leading players in this business, equipped with the education and skills from one of the country’s top institutes and a pioneer in this field. Read More >> About IIMB The Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) believes in building leaders through holistic, transformative and innovative education Read More >> IIMBx IIMB started offering massive open online courses (MOOCs) in 2014 through its digital learning initiative, IIMBx, in partnership with edX – a not-for-profit online initiative of Harvard and MIT. Apart from edX, the programme offers courses on its own platform, IIMBx, and SWAYAM. IIMBx offers MOOCs in all areas of management – data and insights, economics, finance, marketing, people management, operations, and strategy. We also have programs for every kind of learner, ranging from first-generation entrepreneurs to college educators looking to teach better. The IIMBx programme is founded on the philosophy that everyone – irrespective of financial or regional constraints – should have access to quality education. Led by IIMB faculty, IIMBx uses digital learning tools to enable anytime, anywhere learning in a global classroom. IIMBx’ s vision is to create a positive social impact by leveraging educational technology to create a world-class repository of digital courseware in management for learners across the globe. In the long run, IIMBx aims to be a thought leader and preferred digital hub for management education supporting managers, academics and institutions across Asia and Africa. IIMBx, the digital learning initiative of IIMB, is founded on the philosophy that everyone – regardless of their financial, academic, or social backgrounds – should have access to high quality education.  Led by IIMB`s world class faculty, IIMBx started offering Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) in 2014 in partnership with edX – a not for profit online initiative of Harvard and MIT. Today IIMBx courses are available on multiple platforms including SWAYAM, the national learning portal of India, edX and IIMBx (open edX). title: About CenComm | IIMB CenComm
text: About CenComm | IIMB CenComm About Centre for Management Communication The Centre for Management Communication (CMC), one of ten Centres of Excellence at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, focuses on equipping students with persuasive communication skills rooted in creativity, collaboration and empathy. The agile curriculum blends real-world experiences with theoretical insights, giving students a distinct edge as managers. Our highly accomplished faculty include scholars and practitioners from across the globe, who apart from core courses in communication to PGP and PhD students, offer exciting and innovative sessions, workshops and short duration courses to executives and other professionals from Management, Public Policy and Social sectors. From Upskilling Communication Skills to Climate Change to Sustainability to Creative Industries, CMC’s mission is to use best practices of communication to change the world for the better. CMC's foundational ethos is meaningful engagement—connecting academia and industry, research and practice, and executive education with classroom learning. The Centre currently concentrates on three strategic areas: Sustainability and Communication. Health and Crisis Communication. Creative Economy. With these pillars, CMC continues to lead in shaping responsive, responsible, and research-driven communication practices for a rapidly evolving global landscape.

Her teaching and research interests span the fields of media production, creative economy, cultural policy and visual cultures in India with a focus on the politics of empowerment in cultural discourses of women's rights. Her current work explores the intersections between corporate social responsibility and communication for social change. Swati’s writing has appeared in peer-reviewed academic publications like Feminist Media Studies as well as in magazines like Critical Collective and FeministWire . Swati was previously an Assistant Professor in the Department of Communication at St. Joseph’s College, Bangalore, India. From 2010-2014, she worked as Instructor of Film and Media Studies in the Department of Art at Edinboro University of Pennsylvania, USA. She has a PhD in Transnational Studies with a focus in Media Studies as well as an M.F.A in Media Study from the University at Buffalo, the State University of New York, USA. Swati also has an M.A in Mass Communication from the University of Hyderabad, India. In addition, Swati consults on educational technology and pedagogy and is a documentary filmmaker whose films have screened internationally. title: Message from the Chairperson | IIMB CenComm
text: Message from the Chairperson | IIMB CenComm Message from the Chairperson of the Centre Rapid technological advancements, economic and environmental instability, geopolitical risks are only a few of the complexities of today’s global business landscape and pose unprecedented challenges in both Business and Society. The Centre of Management Communication (CMC), one of ten Centres of Excellence at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, is poised to tackle these challenges head on. The CMC’s focus is to equip students with a clear advantage in using persuasive communication techniques with creativity, collaboration, and empathy. We do this with an agile syllabus, combining a dynamic real-life focus with deep theoretical insights. Industry engagements, hands-on projects, a vibrant roster of speakers from various fields of life, are all seamlessly embedded within the curriculum. Our faculty are subject matter experts whose work routinely appears in top peer-reviewed journals and popular publications with global impact. Apart from offering core courses in Communication to our PGP and PhD students, we offer several short and long duration courses across other programs at IIMB, for professionals seeking to further hone their skills. Swati Bandi Our core theme, over the years, has always been meaningful Engagement. We have fostered a robust connection between: Academia and Industry Research and Practice Executive Education and Classroom Teaching and Learning We have 3 major focus areas: Sustainability and Communication Health and Crisis Communication Creative Economy Sustainability and Communication Sustainability and communication are profoundly interconnected. The CMC is well poised to be a key facilitator in bridging the gap between scientific knowledge and public understanding and furthering the conversation. Our roster of activities in the area is robust – sustainability-related global case study competitions, symposiums and panel discussions, publications in academic and popular presses by faculty and many others! Health and Crisis Communication Communicating through uncertainty, in pandemics, business, economy, political factors, or environmental concerns, is another key focus at the CMC. We offer a Massive Open Online Course on Healthcare Communication that teaches participants “communicating about health to different stakeholders, explore various theoretical frameworks and learn practical techniques to enhance your communication strategies.” We encourage dialogue on the topic via podcasts, public discussions, and in-class modules on the topic. Creative Economy Our third focus area is Creative Economy. We at the CMC believe that creative and cultural industries have a crucial role to play in India’s vision of becoming a $5 trillion economy. In 2025, India's Media and Entertainment sector hit INR 2.5 trillion, with digital media transforming content creation and monetization. Indian creative exports, including goods and services, are at about $1.4 trillion, emerging as a key economic driver. With only 8% of India’s population employed in this sector, this share is only expected to grow in line with global forecasts. Aligned with this trend, we have an exciting line up of events: panel discussions, academia - industry partnerships and conferences, apart from film screenings and discussions. Our intention is to make the discussion of Media and Entertainment serious business. Get in touch to collaborate! As you can see, we have a finger on the world’s pulse with a relevant, topical, and dynamic roster of events, and courses driven by an unwavering dedication to teaching excellence. We look forward to welcoming you on campus with renewed energy, passion, and constructive engagement!

title: PGP Core Courses offered by CenComm | IIMB CenComm
text: PGP Core Courses offered by CenComm | IIMB CenComm PGP Core Courses At the Centre of Management Communication (CMC), we believe that effective communication is essential for expressing your thoughts and ideas. Communication skills are a vital component of strategic business management. The ability to analyse problems, develop creative solutions, and articulate them clearly is undoubtedly one of the most important skill sets for a manager. Our course emphasizes honing these communication skills, which include business writing, speaking, reading, listening, and presentation techniques, while adapting to the evolving landscape of management. The Centre of Management Communication (CMC) offers an integrated learning experience through its communication courses, which are spread over the first and second terms of the Postgraduate Programme (PGP). The courses include a Preparatory Programme called the Online Module on Communication (OMC), along with "Advances in Business Communication" in Term 1 and "Communication in the Digital Age" in Term 2. Three core courses are provided to PGP students by the CMC. Program Structure During the first year of the PGP program, students will participate in the following courses: Online Module on Communication (Term 1) Advances in Business Communication (Term 1) Communication in the Digital Age (Term 2) Objectives Our learning objectives for PGP students include: Developing an understanding of the changing nature of business communication. Recognizing the current communication and media landscape, including the functional value of various communication tools. Applying course content to real-world communication challenges faced by organizations. Gaining insights into audience preferences and selecting appropriate communication tools for effective presentations. Identifying the strengths, weaknesses, and barriers of various digital communication channels in a business environment. At the Centre of Management Communication (CMC), we are dedicated to equipping our students with the skills necessary to thrive in today’s dynamic business world. Our communication courses are designed to provide students with the skills to excel in both traditional and digital communication environments by integrating theoretical knowledge with practical application. Course Offerings Online Module on Communication (OMC) The Online Module on Communication (OMC) serves as the foundational course for students, focusing on developing essential communication skills through the Pearson online platform. This module engages students with various assignments, homework, activities, and quizzes, including simulations and writing exercises. OMC begins three weeks before the start of Term 1. The online simulation-based course provides an overview and real-time simulations of effective communication, preparing students for the classroom learning experience in Advances in Business Communication during Term 1. Advances in Business Communication (ABC) In the Advances in Business Communication course, we focus on core concepts of business communication and creating actionable messaging for a shifting global business context. Through interactive, practice-led individual and group sessions, students will learn essential skills for communicating with stakeholders through effective, ethical communication and persuasive business storytelling. We not only teach students to be proficient in business communication but also incorporate real-life scenarios in our in-class activities, making learning more engaging and enjoyable. Communication in the Digital Age (CDA) In the Communication in the Digital Age course, we ensure that students learn to apply these concepts to solve communication challenges faced by actual organizations. This course helps students understand how to select the best message structure and delivery for different digital communication channels. In today’s technology-driven and digitalized world, it is crucial for students to know how to navigate digital environments. In Communication in the Digital Age, we focus on enhancing writing skills, such as persuading through technological communication, collaborating on business writing across global teams, fostering teamwork through effective communication, and establishing accountability and credibility with stakeholders, all through group activities and projects.

title: PGP Elective Courses offered by CenComm | IIMB CenComm
text: PGP Elective Courses offered by CenComm | IIMB CenComm PGP Elective Courses Elective Course offered by CMC: CEO's Agenda - Towards Climate Action In today’s world of accelerating environmental challenges, senior executives are no longer just business leaders—they are strategic catalysts for climate action and resilience. The role of the CEO has evolved, with a clear call to act decisively on climate adaptation and embed sustainability at every level of the organization. This course is designed by Prof. Deepti Ganapathy, member of faculty in IIM Bangalore for students to explore critical questions that define the future of climate-conscious leadership: How can CEOs align their organizational goals with national climate agendas? What strategies enable buy-in across the value chain, especially when building Scope 3 and 4 emissions frameworks? Is ESG a risk to be managed—or a lever for growth? What are the emerging growth dimensions driven by ESG adoption across industries? How is the ESG agenda effectively cascaded throughout an organization? Through interactive sessions, real-world case studies, and guest lectures from industry leaders, participants gain practical insights into how top executives: Craft and execute climate-forward strategies Reduce carbon footprints Champion green innovation Embed sustainability into corporate culture The course also delves into how geopolitical shifts, media narratives, and evolving government regulations influence executive decision-making in the ESG landscape. The elective course is offered by the Centre to the PGP, EPGP and PGPEM programmes. Join us at the forefront of the sustainable business revolution—where climate action isn’t just a responsibility, but a competitive edge. Professor Deepti Ganapathy took the students of the elective class for a field visit at the Toyota Kirloskar Plant, Bengaluru on 2nd February 2025 The BPIM - Switzerland (Business Planning for International Markets) course is an Elective for PGP BPIM - In 2014, IIMB launched a 3-credit course titled Business Planning for International Markets (BPIM) to strengthen internationalization of research and teaching programs. In addition to creating international exposure for students, the initiative helps faculty further their geography-specific research as they interact with local universities, organizations, and research centres. The course involves around 8-10 days of immersion (of which 5 days are business meetings/visits and remaining for understanding the country with respect to its culture, context, and business opportunities).  A few sessions are conducted at IIMB before and after the travel. This year, Professor Deepti Ganapathy and Professor Rusha Das have designed the BPIM to Switzerland.

title: MOOCs | CENCOMM | IIMB
text: MOOCs | CENCOMM | IIMB MOOCs The Centre for Management Communication has been offering a MOOC titled “Health Communication” on the IIMBx platform. Designed and delivered by Professor Deepti Ganapathy, member of the faculty at IIM Bangalore, the course aims to equip healthcare practitioners with essential communication skills across various contexts in health management. The MOOC was first launched on 26 August 2022, as part of the Certificate Programme in Health Management, enrolling over 100 participants. It was offered again on 12 October 2024, and a newly updated version was released for the third time on 24 January 2025. Structured into six modules, the course spans approximately six weeks. Each module includes around 90 minutes of recorded video content, along with assessments, case studies, and discussion forums to facilitate engagement and application of concepts. The curriculum covers key areas such as: Health literacy Message development Cultural competency Digital media in health Interpersonal communication Ethical considerations in health communication To enrich the learning experience, the course features in-depth interviews (each lasting around 45 minutes) with notable experts, including: Dr. Devi Shetty, Chairman and Founder, Narayana Health Professor Roma Subramanian, Health Communication Expert, University of Nebraska at Omaha Additional insights are shared through interviews with: Tina D Purnat, Sunitha Rao, Dr. Neha Pawar, Heeta Lakhani, Dr. Poorvi Bhat, Dr. Usha Rani, Dr. Murlidhara Bhat, and Dr. Rekha Narasimhan. Target Audience: This course is designed for healthcare professionals, public health practitioners, communication specialists, health educators, policymakers, and individuals interested in the field of health communication. It caters to both early-career professionals seeking to enhance their skills and knowledge, as well as experienced professionals aiming to stay updated with the latest communication strategies in public health. This comprehensive and interdisciplinary course continues to contribute meaningfully to the evolving field of health communication. title: PhD Courses | IIMB CenComm
text: PhD Courses | IIMB CenComm PhD Courses Communicating Research — 1 & 2 The Communicating Research modules (Part 1 in Term 3 and Part 2 in Term 6) are integral components of the PhD programme at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore. Together, they strengthen doctoral scholars’ ability to communicate complex research with clarity, coherence, and academic rigour. Communicating Research 1 introduces the essentials of scholarly writing—framing arguments, structuring papers, and presenting data persuasively—while Communicating Research 2 advances these skills through practice in writing for publication, conference presentation, and thesis dissemination. Designed for doctoral students across disciplines, these modules ensure that effective communication becomes a core research competency rather than an afterthought. The sequential design—Part 1 during the coursework phase and Part 2 as students move into independent research—enables a gradual but confident transition from internal academic writing to external scholarly communication. Together, they prepare future researchers and academics to engage diverse audiences and contribute meaningfully to the global body of knowledge.

title: PGPPM Courses | IIMB CenComm
text: PGPPM Courses | IIMB CenComm PGPPM Courses Persuasive Policy Writing — A & B The Persuasive Policy Writing modules (Part A in Term 3 and Part B in Term 6) form a crucial component of the Post Graduate Programme in Public Policy and Management (PGPPM) at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore. Designed to refine the analytical and communication capabilities of experienced policy practitioners, the courses focus on transforming complex evidence and administrative insights into persuasive and actionable policy recommendations. Part A introduces the essentials of structure, clarity, and argumentation, guiding participants to translate research and field data into concise, audience-focused policy briefs and memos. Building on this foundation, Part B advances these competencies through practice-driven learning and global frameworks, emphasizing strategic framing, stakeholder engagement, and high-impact policy communication across diverse governance contexts. These courses are specifically designed for government officials, policymakers, and professionals involved in public policy formulation and implementation. By sequencing the modules across the PGPPM journey—Part A early in Term 3 to strengthen the fundamentals of persuasive writing, and Part B in Term 6 to cultivate advanced strategic communication skills—participants progressively build the capacity to influence decision-making at senior administrative and policy levels. Together, the two modules bridge the gap between policy analysis and policy action, enabling participants to craft writing that informs, persuades, and drives meaningful public outcomes.

title: Testimonials  | CENCOMM | IIMB
text: Testimonials  | CENCOMM | IIMB Testimonials Last month I attended the Global Network Week at IIM Bangalore campus on the CEO's Agenda - Towards Climate Action” led by Prof. Deepti Ganapathy. With 17 years in media and consulting, she’s a powerhouse of knowledge in strategic communication, climate action, and social media. Prof. Deepti brings a multidisciplinary approach to the classroom, bridging corporate strategy, social media, and sustainability. Her journey spans international collaboration with scholars across continents (yes, she’s got a global network from Spain to New Zealand). As co-founder of INDEEP, she also champions social impact beyond academia. Esha Gupta Australian Graduate School of Management, University of New South Wales, participant of the GNAM week. Last month, I had the incredible opportunity to participate in the Global Network for Advanced Management Week at IIM Bangalore. The week focused on critical topics like sustainability and net-zero ambitions, explored through the lenses of business communication, perception, and commitment. Coming from a different background, this experience was new and truly enriching for me. Studying in the IIM environment and learning from the brilliant professor, Deepti Ganapathy, provided a fresh perspective on the challenges and opportunities in sustainability. The diverse mix of students and experts from various industries made the discussions even more insightful and rewarding. A big thank you to Indian Institute of Management Bangalore for organizing such an impactful program, and to all my colleagues for making it so memorable. Excited to apply these learnings and make a meaningful impact! Sanchit Khanna Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, participant of the GNAM week. “It was valuable to get a perspective on how industry thinks about ESG and to hear about the ground reality of how businesses in India evolve, to keep up with Climate Change risks,” Rangoli Gupta Oxford MBA 2023-24 graduate, participant of the GNAM week. The way Prof. Deepti Ganapathy integrates strategic communication with climate action insights is truly inspiring. Your eco takeaways are spot-on, especially the idea of using relatable imagery over fear to motivate action—such a powerful shift in perspective! title: Prof. Deepti Ganapathy delivers a keynote address at the International Conference on Heat and Heatwave Trends and their Health Implications in the Global South
text: Prof. Deepti Ganapathy delivers a keynote address at the International Conference on Heat and Heatwave Trends and their Health Implications in the Global South Prof. Deepti Ganapathy delivers a keynote address at the International Conference on Heat and Heatwave Trends and their Health Implications in the Global South Prof. Deepti Ganapathy delivered the keynote address at the International Conference on Heat and Heatwave Trends and their Health Implications in the Global South, jointly organised by JSS Science and Technology University, NAM S&T Centre, and SCOPE, held from November 6–7, 2025, in Mysore. Prof. Deepti participated as an invited panelist in a session on ‘Developing a Strategic Roadmap for Heatwave Resilience and Health Adaptation in the Global South,’ which discussed collaborative approaches to building climate resilience through communication, policy, and public participation. Her talk, also titled ‘India will bear the brunt of extreme heat conditions, how can media’s representations of this issue spur Climate Action?’ explored the crucial role of the media in shaping public understanding and driving engagement with climate issues. Prof. Deepti highlighted how extreme heat, poor air quality, food insecurity, and mental health challenges not only affect vulnerable communities but also have significant socio-economic and occupational consequences in a developing country like India. Drawing on findings such as The Lancet Countdown report, which noted over 50 additional days of prolonged heat in the past year, she underscored the urgency of accurate and empathetic media reporting. Her address emphasized that linking climate change to public health outcomes can strengthen public engagement and policy response, an aspect that remains underrepresented in current media coverage.

title: Prof. Swati Bandi speaks to Vidya Sanskaar students on the Art of Communication at IIM Bangalore
text: Prof. Swati Bandi speaks to Vidya Sanskaar students on the Art of Communication at IIM Bangalore Prof. Swati Bandi speaks to Vidya Sanskaar students on the Art of Communication at IIM Bangalore Prof. Swati Bandi addressed students from Vidya Sanskaar Pre-University College on the art and practice of communication held at IIM Bangalore on 29 October. In her session, she described communication as a dynamic process that extends beyond reading, writing, speaking, and listening. Highlighting the growing influence of artificial intelligence, she encouraged students to embrace technology as a supportive tool while preserving their authentic voice. Prof. Bandi also reminded the audience that communication is a learned skill rather than an innate talent and urged them to practice consistently, be fearless, and express their individuality with confidence.

title: Prof. Deepti Ganapathy leads valedictory session on Executive Presence for Impactful Leadership
text:
Prof. Deepti Ganapathy leads valedictory session on Executive Presence for Impactful Leadership Prof. Deepti Ganapathy leads valedictory session on Executive Presence for Impactful Leadership A diverse group of senior leaders attended a three-day programme titled 'Executive Presence for Impactful Leadership,' which was led by Prof. Deepti Ganapathy and took place from October 6 to October 8, 2025. The programme provided a transformative journey that encouraged participants to think deeply about their leadership styles and professional impact. It concluded with a valedictory session in which participants synthesised their learnings, examined their changing perspectives, and identified pathways to improve their executive presence. 
Many described the sessions as revelatory and introspective, emphasizing how executive presence transcends industries and roles. Participants recognized that effective leadership is founded on curiosity, courage, and an ongoing commitment to learning and growth.

The twin objectives of the centre to influence policy discourse and improve governance are achieved through rigorous research and stakeholder engagement across domains. Its strong evidence-based research has focused on government innovations, regulation, policy-making, administrative and organizational reform, public-private partnerships and IT in government. A vibrant academic ambience for scholarly engagement has helped CPP emerge as a platform for ideation, debate and exploration. CPP faculty members represent diverse disciplines and research interests. Some of the broad themes of ongoing research projects involving CPP faculty members are: Financial Inclusion, Health, Urban Governance, Gender, Environment and Sustainability, Education, Political Economy, Regulation, Infrastructure and Transportation Systems. CPP engages with a variety of stakeholders/partners. They include Central and State Government agencies, legislative bodies, national and international academic institutions and policy agencies, NGOs, private industry, and individuals. The grant proposal plans to utilize the extensive market data to analyze the lessons emerging from various natural shocks through a market-oriented lens, providing valuable insights into the economic and political history of India during this transformative period. It outlines proposal for bank nationalization in greater detail and also the contours of another angle that focuses on the effects of political uncertainty on economic and financial outcomes. A substantial portion of the grant will be used to digitize data. Once the data is ready after digitization to use and some academic papers are published, the data will be available to other researchers on a request basis. Policy-makers are confronted with difficult choices and have the responsibility of taking crucial decisions which can have significant impacts. Political agendas, socio-economic constraints and global influences play their part in determining which issues get prioritized and which ones take a backseat. Directly or indirectly, and at various levels, they also influence how we choose to address these problems. Decisions about how we deal with such issues are also often based on our experiences, our judgment or professional expertise. In many countries in recent years, there is an increasing trend of shifting from purely opinion-based decision-making to evidence-based practice. Though one must  be wary of using research selectively to justify favored policy positions or push pre-conceived approaches for tackling these issues of concern, it cannot be denied that policies and programmes that draw upon objective, reliable and verifiable research evidence to complement experiential learning are likely to be more successful and effective in achieving the desired results. Towards this objective, the 'Fostering Knowledge-Implementation Links' Project, a joint initiative of the Centre for Public Policy at IIMB, and the Karnataka Health System Development and Reform Project (KHSDRP), has been commissioned as part of the ongoing efforts by the Department of Health and Family Welfare Services, Government of Karnataka, to facilitate greater interaction between different actors working on health issues in the state. It focuses on building bridges between the academic and research community and the government in order to: (i) broaden the evidence base for public health programmes in Karnataka, (ii) identify knowledge gaps in contemporary research on health and health system issues in the state, and (iii) create a more responsive and contextually relevant research agenda to aid policy-making. The project has been engaging with researchers and practitioners to identify high-quality health research from Karnataka, besides using additional library and electronic database searches to supplement the effort, in order to strengthen the evidence base for public health policy and programmes in the state and encourage informed debate and decision-making in policy circles. We have created a repository of policy-relevant research including journal publications, reports, working papers, policy briefs, discussion drafts and reviews that will be a very useful reference to interested researchers and policymakers. A selected choice of policy-relevant research will be presented for discussion during three consultative workshops this year. These workshops will bring together representatives from government, leading academic and research institutions, non-government organizations, professional associations, healthcare providers, independent researchers and consultants working on health issues in the state and provide a forum to share knowledge and experiences, discuss research findings and deliberate on how these can be best translated to succinct policy recommendations that are pragmatic and contextually relevant.

Doctoral-level courses cover research that spans a wide range of sectors and policy areas, both nationally and internationally. Coursework includes analytical methods and tools of research, policy analysis, public administration and law, microeconomics, organizational theory, public and institutional economics. This is in addition to the large number of elective courses offered by faculty. Faculties have expertise and competence to guide research in areas such as public management, health policy, environment, agriculture and rural development, industrial policy, human resources development, infrastructure, regulation, democracy and decentralization, public service delivery, urban governance, public finance and policy modeling. For further details, please visit: https://www.iimb.ac.in/programmes/doctoral-programme Master of Manegment Studies (Public Policy) (MMS(PPP) It aims at strengthening the public policy and managerial skills of future leaders and senior managers from the civil services; and professionals from social, infrastructure and private sectors. Liberalization has blurred the boundary between the public and private as more sectors like infrastructure, utilities and services have got opened up. Private-Public Partnership (PPP) is the new name of the game. It is a unique programme, where professionals from Government and non-government sectors come together in a classroom. It was started to fulfil the need for an educational programme in public policy in India for government officers. It was extended to open candidates in 2008. Considerable synergies exist among private and public sectors, and we expect the classroom experience to enable cross-learning. It proposes to attract overseas participants from the current year, and has added another dimension to the learning experience. For further details, please visit: https://www.iimb.ac.in/programmes/pgppm CEPT-CPP Summer School on The Everyday City Prof. Arnab Mukherji Prof. Kiran Keswani CEPT-CPP Summer School on The Everyday City at the Center for Public Policy, IIM Bangalore from 10th to 25th June 2016 Coordinators: Prof. Arnab Mukherji and Kiran Keswani In India, as in other parts of the world, some of the physical development of the city is influenced by the everyday practices of its people. The urban spaces are continually transformed by social, cultural, religious, political, economic and other practices. Currently, these practices intermingle with each other and with the streets of the city in a random manner. The formal plan finds it difficult to account for these everyday practices due to their changing nature and because they have not been sufficiently documented or analysed. The key question that the summer school on The Everyday City asked was: How can we bring about small changes in our perception and that of others through documenting ‘how people use streets on an everyday basis’? It introduced participants to techniques of observing, recording and representing these informal spaces in order to see and value what often gets left out of planning. The urban practices that were documented during the workshop were analysed through brain-storming sessions as well as discussions on key policy issues that emerged. The CEPT-CPP Summer School was a collaborative effort between CEPT University, Ahmedabad and the Center for Public Policy, IIM-B and was held at the IIM Bangalore campus from 10th to 25th June 2016. The course faculty were Arnab Mukherji, Faculty & Chairperson, and Center for Public Policy and Kiran Keswani, Architect & Urban designer. The Guest faculty were A.Srivathsan, Faculty & Academic Director, CEPT University and Navdeep Mathur, Faculty, Public systems group, IIM Ahmedabad. Outlined below are summaries of the group projects: Complementing or Competing ? A study of formal and informal vendors at Church Street and Brigade Road. This project attempted to understand the behavioural pattern, social relationships and the everyday negotiations between the formal and informal vendors on Church Street and Brigade road in Bangalore. The data collection included activity mapping, interviewing the vendors and representing the data through sketches & maps. The study found that there are pani-puri wallahs, dholak wallahs and vendors selling fashion accessories in front of the high-end branded showrooms and that the two vendor groups both compliment and compete with each other. Thus, formality and informality are found to co-exist whilst vendors serve different economic groups in the city. Group participants: Aarshi Agrawal, Akansha Tiwari & Krupanshi Jha The Street edge as a form of everyday space A study of the footpath along the IIM wall facing Bannerghatta road This study looked at the everyday activities along the footpath abutting the boundary wall of the IIMB campus. It found that in the morning people walk along it on their way to the post office housed within the campus, or to the temple abutting it whilst others use the public toilet that abuts it. During the afternoon, it is used for parking by cab and auto-rickshaw drivers and during the night it is occupied by buses that bring commuters to the call centers and IT offices on Bannerghatta road. It found that the street edge works as an everyday space and concluded that a transition space needs to be designed between the public and private realms that is both functionally and aesthetically better. Group participants: Chirag Manek, Mehar Kochhar, Riddhi Dama & Swati Samantray Samosas @ 10 Negotiations due to appropriation of space during RamzanM This study looked at the ‘Samosa mela’ that takes place every year during the month of Ramzan in the Shivajinagar neighbourhood. Samosas are sold in large numbers at various locations, sometimes encroaching upon footpath space and resulting in spatial negotiations between samosa vendors, pedestrians and vehicles. The study found that the Samosa mela has faced resistance from residents of the neighbourhood due to issues of waste disposal, parking and traffic congestion. Despite the problems, there seems to be strong support for the Mela from both residents and visitors to the area.Thus, a strange relation of illegal yet legitimate activity is generated where the vendors, the public and the governing authorities understand the importance of the Mela and adapt themselves to the changes it brings to the neighbourhood. Group participants:Akshata Bhandiwad, Suyash Bhardway & Drashti Amin In (visible) Formality Street bazaar as a model of collaborative governance This study focused on how the street along the Russell market building in Shivajinagar makes a transition from being a place for tomato auctions in the morning, to a vegetable & fruit bazaar later in the day and a space for paid parking. The study asked two questions: 1. What are the lines of overlap between formality and informality? And 2. How does collaborative governance influence the market? It conducted interviews with both vendors and users finding that there were both informal and formal frameworks that seemed to help sustain the bazaar. It concluded that within what is termed as “Informality” exists a formality which is often not visible. Group participants:Haeli Mehta, Riya Chadha & Nivedha Sarathy
