Transformation of IMR 1986 to 1992 1996 to 2003 2004 to 2009 2010 onwards IIMB Management Review (IMR) launched as biannual in July 1986 with Prof Basu Ghosh as Editor – focus on management applications and public policy in the context of Indian management – 7 volumes published IMR re-launched in 1996 as a quarterly with Vol 8 – Prof. N Balasubramanian, Finance & Accounting, as Chief Editor – repositioned to reach out to management practitioners with all materials being fully researched and validated The IMR Student Essay Competition introduced in 1999 seeking to recognise and reward excellence in management research and writing – the award-winning essays were published in the journal Under the editorship of Prof. B Mahadevan (Production & Operations Management), which commenced with Vol 15 Issue No. 3 September 2003, IMR built on its strengths to position itself as a premier management journal with fresh thinking and newer approaches – focus on conceptual and methodological rigour – increasing refereed content Round Table and Interview features reformatted for rigour of approach, strengthening of academic component while retaining practitioner focus New features introduced – Management Educator’s Forum to explore issues germane to management pedagogy; On the Anvil, a preview of the ongoing research in the field of management Initially open to students of IIMB programmes, in 2003–2004, the fifth edition of the Student Essay Competition was opened to all IIMs, and the following year, 2004–2005, to postgraduate and doctoral students of all Indian management institutions The IMR Conference (IMRC) – theme-based, biennial – launched in 2004 with the aim of bringing together ‘best in class’ practitioners, educators and researchers together to share their knowledge – Selected papers published in IMR The following editions of IMRC were held between 2004 and 2010. IMRC 2004: Innovation: The Next Lever for Value Creation; 17 – 18 Dec 2004 IMRC 2006: Global Competitiveness through Outsourcing: Implications for Services and Manufacturing; 13 – 15 July 2006 IMRC 2008: Global Supply Chain Management: Role of Emerging Economies; 22 – 24 Dec 2008; organised jointly by IMR, the Supply Chain Management Centre, IIMB (SCMC) and the EADS-SMI Chair for Sourcing and Supply IMRC 2010: Global Competitiveness through Human Resource Management; 22 – 24 July 2010 IMR entered into an agreement with EBSCO, leading online database for dissemination of content, May 2003 – Dec 2009 On the Technology front, the following innovations were made: Compact Disc (CD) version of journal introduced with Vol 16-2, June 2004 --Back Issues from 1996 available in set of two CDs Journal tracker to track progress of articles, maintain database of contributors and referees Subscription package to maintain database of subscribers and track renewals IMR Conference website designed and maintained Prof. V Ravi Anshuman (Finance & Accounting) took over as Chief Editor with  Vol 19 No 4, December 2007 IMR initiated and instituted the country's first annual doctoral students conference for management scholars in 2009. The first IMR Doctoral Conference (IMRDC) was held on 27th November 2009 – IMRDC aimed to recognise quality research in management in India carried out by doctoral students; to alert and sensitize young scholars to the pursuit of rich research opportunities in the Indian context and to encourage them to pursue these opportunities. Today, IMRDC has grown into a milestone event for Indian and international doctoral students featuring select paper presentations, keynote lectures and invited talks, panel discussions, and workshops from leading researchers, academics and practitioners in the field. From world-class postgraduate and doctoral programmes to new advances in multidisciplinary undergraduate education, our vision is clear: global excellence rooted in purpose and impact.

title: About the IIMB Development Foundation | Giving | IIMB
text: About the IIMB Development Foundation | Giving | IIMB About IIMB Development Foundation The IIMB Development Foundation (IDF) is IIMB’s official fundraising and development arm established in 2024 as a Section 8 (non-profit) company. IDF plays a pivotal role in mobilising philanthropic support to advance IIMB’s mission of excellence in management education, research, and innovation. IDF is dedicated to building meaningful partnerships with alumni, corporates, foundations, and individual donors who are passionate about transforming education in India. Contributions through the Foundation support critical initiatives such as: Scholarships and financial aid for deserving students Faculty chairs and research funding Infrastructure development including state-of-the-art learning spaces Entrepreneurship and innovation programs Sustainability and social impact projects All donations are made directly to IIM Bangalore. Serving as the Institute’s dedicated fundraising and development wing, IDF ensures contributions are aligned with strategic priorities.

text: Support Excellence, Diversity, & Research | IIMB Giving IIMB Vision IIMB is committed to building leaders who can move the world forward. Our work begins with a clear purpose. We invest in talent, strengthen research, and expand opportunity. We are growing our faculty, deepening international links, and scaling up entrepreneurial efforts. Today, we are home to 110 full-time faculty and 240 staff members. Around 1,505 students are enrolled in our degree programmes. More than 6,000 professionals participate in Executive Education each year. Your support will help take this further. It opens doors, drives research, and brings ideas to life. Together, we create value that reaches across sectors and borders. Academic Excellence 11 disciplines. 10 centres of excellence. One mission – advancing knowledge. Your contribution helps IIMB deepen research, expand learning, and preserve a tradition of academic excellence that lasts generations. Research Advancement Great ideas begin with bold questions. IIMB’s faculty pursue research that challenges conventions and sparks change – from boardrooms to government policy. Your support helps turn this knowledge into impact. Access and Diversity IIMB’s financial self-sufficiency opens doors to bold ideas — but this strength requires ongoing support. Your assistance ensures we meet this responsibility, enabling us to innovate, include, and inspire across all we do. Leadership Development Since 1973, IIMB has prepared students to lead with purpose. We did this by offering one doctoral and four master’s programmes. Our work doesn’t stop in the classroom, we continue to engage with government, industry, and communities to grow talent that can make a difference. Your support powers this mission. It helps students grow into leaders who drive innovation, solve real problems, and shape the future.

title: Scholarships, Financial Aid & Student Support | IIMB Giving
text: Scholarships, Financial Aid & Student Support | IIMB Giving Scholarships At IIMB, we aspire to ensuring that no student offered admission is denied access to a high-quality management education due to financial constraints. Need-based scholarships of up to 100% are awarded to deserving candidates based on income level and demonstrated financial need. Additionally, merit-based scholarships are offered to exceptionally talented students to recognize and support academic excellence. To strengthen and expand these student-support initiatives, we invite your generous contributions – whether through an endowment or by directly funding scholarships for selected students. Your support can help transform lives and advance inclusive, world-class education at IIM Bangalore. Type of Scholarships Directors Merit List Directors Merit List (DML) is a scholarship that is given to the top 5% of the batch at the end of the first year of PGP programme Differently-abled 5% of the admissions intake has been reserved for students with disability (around 25 students per year). Based on need the scholarships covering 20%, 50% or 100% of the fees are given to these students Merit Scholarships This is based on academic performance. Can be given subject-wise NSR Pre-Doctoral Fellowship The Prof. N. S. Ramaswamy Pre-Doctoral Fellowship is a highly selective programme instituted with the aim to increase social diversity of management academia in India. It is a flexible one-year apprenticeship, designed to help the selected pre-doctoral fellows successfully apply to doctoral programmes in management and allied disciplines. The program specifically targets applicants from historically underrepresented sections of the society Public Policy Scholarships In order to promote the public policy programme, IIMB seeks to institute scholarships to students who are keen on pursuing public policy but are not in a position to pay the course fee. This is a need-based scholarship Ph.D Ph.D students spend 5-6 years to complete their programme. Through this period, IIMB supports the students at an average cost of Rs 55,000 per month. Despite constraints, IIMB is committed to research and has an average intake of 20+ students every year. At any time on campus, we have close to 100+ fellows at different stages of their programme. The fellowship amount is Rs. 6.6 lakhs/fellow/year Give Back Today

title: IIMB Donor Recognition: Naming Rights & Donor Wall of Fame
text: IIMB Donor Recognition: Naming Rights & Donor Wall of Fame All donations to IIMB are gratefully acknowledged and appropriately recognised. Individuals, corporations, and organizations making significant financial contributions may be accorded naming rights in their honour – for  a School, Centre of Excellence, Building or Facility, Endowed Professorship, Scholarship Fund, etc. To explore specific giving opportunities, please contact us at idf@iimb.ac.in or call us at +91 80 2699 3157. We’d be happy to guide you on how your support can make a meaningful impact. In appreciation of their support, all donors are also recognised in the appropriate tier on the IIMB Donor Wall of Fame. Furthermore, all contributions to IIMB are eligible for 100% tax deduction under Section 80G of the Income Tax Act. IIMB is exempt from the provisions of the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA). Donations received in the USA are tax-deductible. DONOR WALL OF FAME At IIMB, we are deeply grateful to all our donors who have generously contributed to various causes that support our mission in education, research, and social impact. To honour their commitment, we have created a Virtual Donor Wall of Fame to recognize individuals and organizations who have made significant financial contributions. In addition to the virtual wall, we also have physical donor walls located at the Pergola on the IIMB campus, which proudly display the names of our esteemed benefactors. These walls serve as a lasting tribute to the generosity of our donors and their role in shaping the future of IIM Bangalore.

title: Donor Messages | IIMB
text:
Donor Messages | IIMB Donor Messages We invited several of our generous donors to share their experience at IIMB and to describe what inspired them to give back to the Institute. Here’s what they had to say about the impact of IIMB on their lives and why supporting the next generation of leaders matters to them. Parag Dhol PGP 1991-1993 In the three odd decades since I graduated, I have realised that I am a keen, and ongoing, student of business (did not know this when I registered for my MBA!). IIM Bangalore set-up the foundation for that journey. I am eternally grateful for what I learnt there as well as the calibre of people I met there. Snehal Shah PGP 1993-1995 Partner Fairwinds Private Equity Being an alumnus of one of the top education institutions in Asia, provided me a platform to pursue a career of my choice and shape it well. I strongly believe that each and every person is entitled to get a high-quality education. However, there are many deserving students who are not able to get access to higher education in world-class institutes due to financial constraints. It’s my endeavor to support them in whatever way I can and I am grateful to my alma mater IIMB which has enabled me to do so. I wish all the very best to IIMB and the current and future generation of students Sangeet Paul Choudary PGP 2004-2006 Founder, Platformation Labs I will forever remain indebted to IIMB. IIMB has been the gift that keeps giving - it provided me with the education, launchpad, and peer network to excel in a highly fulfilling career. Being a part of the IIMB ecosystem has been my privilege. My contribution to the institute is a humble attempt to give back a little from where I have gained so much. I hope that just as the institute transformed my life and career, my contribution can further the institute's cause as it transforms the lives and careers of many more. Shashi Yadavalli PGP 1996-1998 Principal, Deloitte Consulting Hearty congratulations to IIMB for the upcoming 50th year anniversary. I am forever indebted to the Institution for equipping me with the skills and recognition to be a Business Leader. I wish all the very best to IIMB in the future endeavors and growth pathways. Dinesh Khanna & Deeptha Khanna PGP 1996-1998 It is no exaggeration to say that IIM Bangalore changed our lives. For young 20+ olds growing up in military families, the institute opened up a world of business and opportunity that we had no understanding of. IIMB equipped us with core skills - analytical rigor, clarity in communication, strong strategic constructs, how to collaborate and work effectively in organizations..and even while we didn't realize it then, the muscle memory of this rigor helped us every step of our careers. But IIM Bangalore is special to us for more than the expected. It is also where we met, 26 years ago; and where our parents on both sides met, as we graduated. This is where our very own Two States story was written. It is to honor the profound impact IIMB has had - not just on us, but on our two families, that we were delighted to offer a contribution in the name of our parents. We are thrilled with IIMB's commitment to expand their platform to reach and shape even more lives. Congratulations and Thank you. Rajeev Chaba President and Managing Director, MG Motor India Pvt. Ltd. I feel very blessed to be able to support the institute in my own small way to achieve their objective. Education and gender parity are two of the key pillars for the future progress of the country. I would do my best to keep supporting these areas. I want to thank the institute to help me reach today where I am to facilitate the objective. Ramdas Baliga Bantwal Managing Director, Toshiba Software India Toshiba Software India is an intrinsic part of the Toshiba Group’s digital and software transformation worldwide. As the world shift towards digital transformation at an accelerated pace, we aim to empower digital agility across and beyond Toshiba, evolving TSIP into a Digitally Agile Centre of Excellence. TSIP’s deliveries tie very well into Toshiba’s goal of applying Digital Technologies across Physical systems, where Toshiba is already a world Leader, thereby realizing leadership in Cyber Physical Systems. Grounded in the Group’s commitment of “Committed to People, Committed to the Future.”, we are building a robust team of engineers who will acquire and expand their skillset working on advanced Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and IoT technologies. Rishi Kulkarni Co - Founder at Revv.so/RevvSales (Acquired by LegalZoom); Founder 1Click (Acquired by Freshworks) I'm forever indebted to NSRCEL at IIMB. They gave my startup and me an opportunity 10 years ago which made me the entrepreneur I'm today.
NSRCEL & IIMB have continued to make a bigger and bigger impact on the startup community at large. I will continue to support IIMB's initiatives financially and otherwise. Debajyoti Ray Chaudhuri MD & CEO National E-Governance Services Limited National E-Governance Services Limited (NeSL) is an Information Utility regulated by The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) under the provisions of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). One of the objectives behind creation of the IU was to remove information asymmetry which in the Indian context is often a critical barrier to fair negotiations between debtor and creditor when creditor is unable to service its debt obligations. The IU as conceptualised in the Code has no parallel anywhere in the world.
NeSL’s Digital Document Execution or DDE platform provides for digital execution, storage and access of contracts. It marks a paradigm shift towards a seamless but secure digital lending as its e-stamped as per legal requirements. It’s paperless, contactless and enhances the customer experience. It also promotes sustainability by obviating the need for paper. As per our estimates, till date, NESL’ s DDE has saved more than 2500 trees.
It’s therefore quite appropriate that we promote cleaner and environment friendly transport systems. The EV Charging station at IIM Bangalore, funded by us as part of our CSR Activity, was inaugurated on the 23rd of February, 2023 by Hon’ble President NCLT, Chief Justice (Retd) Shri Ramlingam Sudhakar in the august presence of Hon’ble Justice Kannan Ramesh, Judge, Appellate Division, Supreme Court of Singapore and Judge, Singapore International Commercial Court, Chairperson IBBI, Shri Ravi Mital, Prof. Rishikesha T Krishnan, Director, IIM Bangalore, Whole Time members of IBBI, Shri Sudhaker Shukla and Shri Jayanti Prasad, EDs of IBBI, ED of NeSL Smt E. P. Nivedita, team NeSL and a host of Other dignitaries.
As on date it’s IIM B’s only EV Charging station with fast charge facility. Ritesh Patel Head Of Compliance at Mirae Asset Investment Managers (India) Mirae Asset Foundation has always been committed and supported high achievers for promoting excellence in education in India and providing opportunities to disadvantaged students to pursue their dreams.
We are proud to be associated with IIM Bangalore since last 5 years to pursue this vision and have been supporting the PGP and doctorate students at IIM Bangalore through Mirae Asset Foundation Scholarship program.
Through the partnership with one of the global, renowned academic institution such as IIM Bangalore, Mirae Asset Foundation aims to promote excellence in education, encourage innovation and entrepreneurship and help passionate young people to attain the knowledge and experience they need to spread their wings and create bright future for our society. Anurag Pratap Vice President, Digital Inclusion & Sustainability Leader Capgemini India Capgemini has always considered itself a front-runner in the Digital Transformation space by ensuring that technology and innovation can be leveraged to create sustainable solutions and an equitable society for all. Our Digital Inclusion program relies on two pillars: bridging the digital divide and using technology to ensure social and sustainable development for everyone.
We are able to fulfil this commitment in a major way through our partnership with IIM-B’s NSRCEL initiative as this venture allows start-ups, co-working ventures, eminent academicians from its parent institution IIM-B, and researchers, to build an active support ecosystem for early-stage entrepreneurs and thus act as an incubator for new business ideas. Helping support early-stage social ventures with innovative solutions to tackle the country’s pressing social problems through scalable and sustainable business models helps us maintain our commitment towards a sustainable and equitable future for all.
Capgemini truly supports the entrepreneurial mindset we have witnessed in each of these social ventures and truly hopes this partnership with IIM-B will help created a significant and long-lasting impact on our society. Harsh Mariwala Founder and Chairman of Marico Ltd Innovation continues to be an essential catalyst and a critical driver for economic growth, especially for emerging economies like India. Many leading and ‘future ready’ organisations are now focusing on an enabling culture and a reward and recognition mechanism to drive innovation. A lot of successful legacy organisations are fostering an innovation-based culture and have ‘institutionalised’ innovation within the organisation and among the stakeholders. Start-ups in India are creating a vibrant eco-system for innovation to thrive.
We believe that education and research plays a major role in driving innovation in the society. And this is where institutions like IIM Bengaluru can contribute significantly to the cause. With the larger aim of advancement of Research and Teaching in the areas of innovation and leadership, in 2021, we instituted the Ram Charan Chair at IIM Bengaluru. I am sure with our combined vision of fuelling innovation and leadership, the Ram Charan Chair will contribute immensely to enriching management education and driving innovation capability amongst Indian organisations.

title: Frequently Asked Questions | IIMB Development Foundation (IDF)
text: Frequently Asked Questions | IIMB Development Foundation (IDF) Frequently Asked Questions(FAQs) About IIMB Development Foundation What is the IIMB Development Foundation (IDF)? The IIMB Development Foundation (IDF) was set up in 2024 as a Section 8 (non-profit) Company with the sole objective of assisting the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) in its fundraising efforts. IDF strives to ensure that all philanthropic activities, by existing and prospective donors, are conducted in a professional manner in line with IIMB’s mission, vision and strategic plans. How is IDF connected to IIMB? IDF was created to support and advance IIMB’s mission through fundraising, strategic partnerships, and alumni engagement. While IDF operates independently for administrative purposes, it works closely with the Institute and serves as its official fundraising and development arm. IDF’s team operates from the IIMB Campus. What is IDF’s mission and purpose? Driven by IIMB’s commitment to excellence, inclusivity, and nation-building, IDF supports a range of initiatives that make education accessible and strengthen the Institute. These include scholarships and financial aid for deserving students, support for faculty chairs and research, development of state-of-the-art learning spaces, entrepreneurship and innovation programs, and sustainability and social impact projects. Why does IIMB need funds? To enable its commitment to shaping responsible leaders, supporting groundbreaking research, and fostering inclusive growth, IIMB relies on sustained support. This is especially true after IIMB gained greater autonomy under the 2017 IIM Act – this came with the responsibility of being financially self-sufficient. While the independence fuels innovation and excellence, it also means that creating impact at scale now depends on the generosity of donors. By supporting IIMB, you become part of a vibrant mission to deliver world-class education and strengthen one of India’s most respected institutions — today and for the future, in particular for the new Undergraduate IIMB School of Multidisciplinary Studies. Donations & Fund Use Am I donating to IIMB or to IDF? All donations are made directly to IIM Bangalore, and remittances go directly to the bank account of IIM Bangalore. The remittances are not routed through IDF – IDF merely serves as the official fundraising and development arm of the Institute, helping to channel contributions toward key priorities areas. For what purpose is my donation being used? Your donation is used to support strategic initiatives at IIM Bangalore, including scholarships for deserving students, faculty endowments, infrastructure development, research and innovation, and new academic programs such as the upcoming Undergraduate School of Multidisciplinary Studies. Every contribution is directed toward initiatives that strengthen the Institute’s mission of academic excellence, inclusion, and global impact. Can I choose the cause to which my donation is applied? You can specify your preference in the comments section from the available options when making a donation to IIM Bangalore: Individual Contribution Batch Contribution Saksham Naming a Hostel Room Naming a Stone Block in a Hostel Room How are the funds utilised if I make an “Individual Contribution”? The funds will be applied by IIM Bangalore towards Scholarships, Chair Professorships, Research Initiatives, Construction, Repairs & Maintenance of Physical Infrastructure in the Bannerghatta Road campus and the new Undergraduate IIMB School of Multidisciplinary Studies. What does a “Batch Contribution” mean? Contributions will be recognised by IIM Bangalore in aggregate across your respective batch, categorized by program and graduating year (e.g., 'PGP 2025', 'PGPEM 2025', etc. Tax & Legal Will I receive a tax exemption certificate (like 80G)? Yes. After your donation is processed, you will receive a Section 80G tax exemption certificate, which serves as official proof for claiming tax benefits. I live outside India. Can I donate, and will I get any tax benefits? Yes, individuals residing outside India can donate to IIMB. The Institute is exempt from the provisions of the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA), which enables it to legally receive foreign donations. If you are a U.S. tax resident, your contribution will be made to the IIM Bangalore Educational Foundation (IIMB EF), an entity registered under Internal Revenue Code Section 501(c)(3) the U.S.A. and are hence eligible for 100% tax exemption. Please write to us at idf@iimb.ac.in or call us at +91 80 2699 3157, and the team will guide you through the documentation and process. I am not an alumnus of IIMB, can I donate? Yes, you can! Donations are welcome from anyone who wishes to support the mission and vision of IIMB. Do donations to IIMB qualify under the CSR provisions of the Companies Act, 2013? Yes, IIMB is an eligible institution under the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) provisions of the Companies Act, 2013. Contributions made through your company’s CSR program can support initiatives such as education, research, social impact projects, and infrastructure development. If your organization is interested in partnering through CSR, please write to us at idf@iimb.ac.in or call us at +91 80 2699 3157, and the team will guide you through the process. How to Give How can I donate? You can make your contribution via Demand Draft, Cheque, Wire Transfer, Debit/Credit Card, Net Banking, or UPI. Can I make pledges or recurring donations? Yes, that’s possible. Please email us at idf@iimb.ac.in or call us at +91 80 2699 3157. We will be happy to discuss the terms and conditions and proceed with signing an MoU to take this forward. What payment options are available for donors outside India? If you reside outside India and wish to contribute to IIMB, please reach out to us at idf@iimb.ac.in or call us at +91 80 2699 3157. We’ll be happy to assist you with the process. I faced technical difficulties while making an online donation. Who can I contact for assistance? If you experience any technical issues while making an online donation, please email us at idf@iimb.ac.in or call us on +91 80 2699 3157. Our team will be happy to assist you and ensure your contribution is processed smoothly. Donor Engagement Will I get immediate confirmation of the receipt of funds? Yes, the receipt will be sent to your registered email for all successful payments made through the payment gateway. For contributions made via cheque or demand draft, the receipt will be shared after confirmation by our back-end team. I have seen classrooms in IIMB named after donors. Can I also obtain naming rights to a classroom or other facility by donating to IIMB? Yes, you can obtain naming rights for a classroom or other facilities by contributing the designated amount associated with each. Can donations be made in honour or memory of a parent, batchmate, or faculty member? Yes, donations can be made in honour or memory of a parent, batchmate, or faculty member. To do so, please select ‘Others’ under the ‘Donated by’ option on the payment page and include the relevant details in the ‘Comments’ field. Alternatively, you can contact us at idf@iimb.ac.in or call us on +91 80 2699 3157 for assistance. Scholarships & Impact How are the recipients of the scholarships selected? Can I play a role in the selection process? The recipients for the scholarships are selected after a rigorous and thorough process by the Institute’s Admissions and Financial Aid Committee. For sponsored scholarships that meet the designated amount, donors may be involved in the selection process. For more information, please contact us at idf@iimb.ac.in or call us on +91 80 2699 3157. Data & Privacy Is my donation and personal information secure? Yes, your donation and personal information are completely secure. We use trusted and encrypted payment gateways that comply with industry-standard security protocols (like SSL) to ensure your data is protected. We do not store your payment details, and your personal information is kept confidential and used only for necessary communication or legal compliance. Get in Touch Who can I contact for more information or specific queries? For any questions, clarifications, or additional information regarding donations, partnerships, or initiatives, please feel free to reach out to us at idf@iimb.ac.in or call us on +91 80 2699 3157. Our team at the IIMB Development Foundation will be happy to assist you.

Additional Information At the moment, Prof Das is UNABLE to offer internships, summer or winter research projects to students from outside IIM Bangalore. Accomplishments RESEARCH TEACHING CONSULTING AWARDS SERVICE EDUCATION His major research domains are Statistical Methods, Actuarial Mathematics and Operations Research. Specific topics of interests include Multivariate Statistics, Statistical Analysis of Fuzzy data, Sports Analytics, Business Forecasting, Measurement and Scaling and Discrete Optimization problems. Professor Das has published several papers in refereed journals of international repute. He co-authored a book titled Facing the Future: Indian Pension Systems’ and also co-authored the chapter on Canonical Correlations in the Encyclopedia of Biostatistics. Besides these, he has published technical reports and delivered seminars at various international conferences. SIGNIFICANT PUBLICATIONS: Alarm System for Insurance Companies: A Strategy for Capital Allocation, S. Das and M. Kratz . Insurance: Mathematics and Economics  51 (2012) 53-65. Joint Life Insurance Policies with Differential Benefits and Premiums to the Policyholders, S. Das (2008) Asia-Pacific Journal of Risk and Insurance 2(2) pp 1-18. On Measuring Imprecision in Human Response due to Respondent and Attribute and its Utility in Questionnaire Design, S. Das (2006), International Journal of Uncertainty and Knowledge-based Systems.14(2). Binary Knapsack Problems with Random Budgets, S. Das and D. Ghosh (2003), J. of Operational Research Society 54 (9): pp 970-983. Quantifying fuzziness due to the scale of measurement in response systems, S. Das (2002), Fuzzy Sets and Systems 132: pp 317-333. Restricted Canonical Correlations, S. Das and P.K.Sen (1994), Linear Algebra and Its Applications 210: pp 29-47. Besides teaching the core courses on Statistics for the post-graduate programmes, doctoral programme and various executive education programmes at IIMB, he offers elective courses on Business Forecasting, Sports Analytics, Insurance Analytics and Actuarial Mathematics. Chairperson, QM & IS Area, 2012-14 Chairperson, Admissions, 2005-2007 Chairperson, Library, 2001-2003 Professor Das engages in training and other consultancy services in the domain of Business Statistics, Business Analytics, Advanced Market Research, Business Forecasting, and Insurance with various prominent companies in the country. He received the best paper award in the 7th APRIA for work on Joint life Insurance Policy with Differential Benefit and Premium. Read More >> About IIMB The Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) believes in building leaders through holistic, transformative and innovative education Read More >> Faculty profiles Arjun Ramachandra Home Faculty Arjun Ramachandra Assistant Professor Decision Sciences IIMB Young Faculty Research Chair Connect with Faculty arjun.ramachandra@iimb.ac.in Curriculum Vitae Personal Website Blog Summary Arjun Ramachandra is an Assistant Professor in the Decision Sciences area at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore. My research interests broadly lie in optimization under uncertainty at the interface of operations research, probability theory and computer science focusing on leveraging tools from these areas to efficiently solve or derive performance guarantees to complex optimization problems. Specific thrust areas with an interdisciplinary flavour include distributionally robust optimization, data-driven tail risk estimation, theory of negative dependence, correlation gap analysis with weak independence, approximation guarantees with submodularity and derandomization with small sample space constructions. My current research is aimed at analyzing challenging discrete optimization problems to develop novel insights into the behaviour of structured function classes under realistic notions of randomness. My work has found applications in areas such as bottleneck combinatorial optimization, data-driven portfolio optimization and project evaluation and review techniques (PERT) for managers. I hold a joint Ph.D. in Operations Research from the National University of Singapore and Singapore Institute of Technology and Design. Prior to my doctoral stint, I have several years of undergraduate teaching experience after graduating with an Integrated Master’s degree in Maths and Computing from the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur. Aside from work, you can find me immersed in meditation, soulful singing (accompanied by the harmonium), philosophical contemplation or a jolly good daddy's day out entertaining my kids! Accomplishments RESEARCH AWARDS EDUCATION Research Interests: Distributionally robust optimization, data-driven tail risk estimation, theory of negative dependence, correlation gap analysis with weak independence, approximation guarantees with submodularity, and derandomization with small sample space constructions. Publications: Extremal Probability Bounds in Combinatorial Optimization, with Divya Padmanabhan, Selin Damla Ahipasaoglu and Karthik Natarajan, SIAM Journal on Optimization, 32(4), 2828-2858, 2022. Robust Conic Satisficing, with Napat Rujeerapaiboon and Melvyn Sim, preprint available on arXiv (2107.06714). His research focuses on the optimization of transportation networks and supply chain operations, with an emphasis on practical concerns such as equitable workload allocation. He employs a range of methodologies, including integer programming, neural combinatorial optimization, machine learning, and heuristic approaches. His work has been published in leading journals such as Transportation Science , Computers & Operations Research , and Annals of Operations Research , and has been recognized at international conferences, including being a finalist for the Best Paper Award at the 2024 IISE Annual Conference. Prior to joining IIMB, Shankar worked in the IT industry around Cambridge, USA. At Sapient, he consulted with clients in energy and healthcare. He then moved to Curl Corporation, an MIT start-up, where he built bandwidth-efficient applets.  At Reuters Consulting, he worked with financial firms as a solutions architect. Shankar has strived to extend the reach of education with technology. He has anchored a program for school mathematics called Topper TV. His MOOCs on business statistics are featured on edX. As the IT Chair during the pandemic, he helped repurpose IIMB classrooms to reach students everywhere. Shankar is interested in data science, healthcare, and agile methods. He teaches courses in big data analytics and information systems management. He currently directs the DSAI program, which focuses on data science. He has created and directed the GMHE program, which is aimed at healthcare professionals. Shankar holds a doctorate in mathematics and a masters in computer science from Georgia Tech. These include Behavioral Economics, Development Economics, Game Theory, Industrial Organization, International Trade, Labour Economics, Monetary Economics and Public Economics. Research Overview Fiscal and monetary policies are key levers of economic management. How does their interplay influence inequality and income distribution? Doctoral student Kunal Biswas, Economics area, examines how policy coordination impacts macroeconomic stability and consumption inequality. Using a novel empirical measure and a DSGE framework calibrated to India, his research reveals how expansionary shocks redistribute consumption across households, offering insights into the nuanced trade-offs in economic policy design. View more Research Spotlight Video's As economies evolve, so do the skills that shape both traditional and entrepreneurial labour markets. How do workers’ skills interact with economic forces to influence mobility, venture success, and long-term workforce participation? Economics area PhD scholar Sabhya Rai explores the role of skill endowments, accumulation, and depreciation in shaping career trajectories. From sectoral shifts in India to the entrepreneurial learning curve and women’s labour market participation in the U.S., her research uncovers hidden forces driving employment dynamics in a changing world. Economic activity is unevenly distributed across regions and across variables such as income, output, growth, and unemployment. Yet policy often takes a one-size-fits-all approach. To that end, how does location influence industrial growth, trade, and inequality? Doctoral scholar Vivek Kandimalla, Economics area, narrows his focus to India’s manufacturing sector through spatial economics, studying how industrial policies impact regional welfare and how trade barriers drive inefficiencies. Date Speaker Title Sep 11 Shweta Oct 16 Sabhya Essays on Skills and Labor Market Outcomes Oct 30 Vivek Nov 13 Shivali Sharma Unlocking Opportunities: Exploring the Socioeconomic Dynamics of Market Access and Financial Inclusion Nov 17 Kunal Biswas Essays on Fiscal-Monetary Linkages Jan 29 Vandana Feb 19 Suchetan Mar 05 Teena and Usha Past Brown Bag Seminar July 18, 2025, Pradyun Rame Mehrotra and Prof. Tirthatanmoy Das Title Work-From-Home Revolution: Enhancing Women’s Participation in STEM Abstract Women remain persistently underrepresented in STEM occupations despite sustained organizational efforts to improve retention and gender diversity. In this context, we examine whether increased work-from-home (WFH) opportunities raise young women’s participation in STEM roles. Leveraging data from IPUMS-CPS, SWAA, and job postings, and drawing on theories from labor economics and organizational strategy, we implement a Difference-in-Differences design that exploits unanticipated occupation-level variation in WFH adoption induced by the COVID-19 pandemic. We find that high WFH adoption increases the probability of STEM employment among young women by 2.43 percentage points, a 13.6 percent increase relative to the pre-pandemic baseline. The effect is robust to various clustering levels, treatment intensity definitions, matched samples, and other validity checks. The results strongly indicate that the effect operates through reduced skill loss, enabled by increased labor market attachment under WFH adoption. Moreover, the impact varies across STEM subfields and industries and rises with the intensity of WFH adoption. As such, these findings identify WFH as a scalable organizational strategy for improving female retention and advancing DEI in high skill occupations.

His research areas are Industrial Organization, Antitrust Economics, and Information Economics. His current research focuses on antitrust and regulatory issues in the digital markets. He uses game-theoretic modeling as an analytical tool to understand the economic behavior of online firms. He has a Ph.D. in Economics from Indian Statistical Institute, Masters in Economics from Delhi School of Economics, and a Bachelor of Arts in Economics from Sri Ram College of Commerce. Before his doctoral studies, he worked as an Economist at the Competition Commission of India, New Delhi. Jha is Professor of Entrepreneurship at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) and Chairperson of NSRCEL, IIMB’s startup incubator. Her research interest is in Innovation and Entrepreneurship in the emerging country context. She has published papers in several top-tier international journals and has co-edited a book titled “Shifting Orbits: Decoding the Trajectory of the Indian Startup Ecosystem”. She works closely with many startups, mentoring and advising them. She has also contributed to policy formulation around innovation and entrepreneurship at the international, national and state government levels. In 2018, he served as a Post-Doctoral Researcher in Entrepreneurship at the School of Entrepreneurship of the Spears School of Business of Oklahoma State University. His research interests are entrepreneurial cognition and affect, alertness, family business, time perspective, mixed methods, and venture capital. In 2016, he received his Ph.D. in Management from Paris Sciences et Lettres-Université Paris-Dauphine. He is a member of the Entrepreneurship Division of the Academy of Management. He is an editorial board member of Academy of Management Perspectives , Venture Capital , and Small Business Economics . He published in journals such as Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice , Strategic Entrepreneurship Journal , Journal of Organizational Behavior , British Journal of Management , Small Business Economics , Journal of Business Research , and Asia Pacific Journal of Management . I primarily use an organizational theory lens, and specifically a network theory and method lens. My prior research has been published in American Journal of Sociology, Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice, Journal of Business Ethics , and Asia-Pacific Journal of Management . I teach entrepreneurship at the MBA and executive education level, and I also coordinate our 6-month long certificate program for family businesses . At the doctoral level, I teach a course on Network theory and analysis , and I also teach a classical sociological theory course, which covers Weber, Marx, Durkheim, Mead, Foucault, Bourdieu, Goffman, Fanon etc. I did my PhD in Sociology from the University of Minnesota (2010), and then worked in HEC Paris France as an Assistant Professor on the tenure track from 2010-2016, before moving to IIMB, India. Prior to doing my PhD, I worked in ICICI Ltd. Before pursuing a doctorate, she worked in ICICI Ltd., and has been involved in several start-ups in an advisory role. Her research interests are at the intersection of entrepreneurship, strategic management, and digital technologies. She studies digital platform ecosystems, focusing on platform-dependent entrepreneurs and platform scope. She also examines accelerators and their implications for new ventures.  Ramya has presented her research at international conferences and received accolades for her work. Her research is published in the Journal of Management Studies, a leading peer-reviewed journal, and other outlets. Prior to pursuing her doctoral studies, Ramya spent a decade in the software industry, working in technology and management roles. Drawing on her industry experience and education, she teaches courses on entrepreneurship, digital strategy and transformation, and strategic management at doctoral, MBA, and executive education levels. His research interests are in corporate governance, nonmarket strategies, and meta-analysis. He studies these issues in the context of international business, strategic CSR, and entrepreneurship. Sai earned his B.Com (Hons.), M.B.A. (Finance), and M.Phil (Management) from the Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Learning, and Ph.D. from the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (IIMA). He is a joint recipient of the Prof. Tirath Gupta Memorial Thesis Award in 2019 for his doctoral thesis titled “Essays on the internal markets of business groups”. Before joining the doctoral programme at IIMA, Sai served as an Assistant Professor at the Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Learning and as a Guest Faculty at IIMB. Sai has presented his research at several international conferences such as the Strategic Management Society Annual Conference, Academy of Management Annual Meeting, Academy of International Business Annual Meeting, 7th Israel Strategy Conference, and Strategic Management Society Special Conference in India. A paper based on his doctoral thesis was shortlisted for the GSJ Best Paper Award at the SMS Special Conference in India. Read More >> About IIMB The Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) believes in building leaders through holistic, transformative and innovative education Read More >> Faculty profiles Varun Jindal Home Faculty Varun Jindal Assistant Professor Finance & Accounting Connect with Faculty varun.jindal@iimb.ac.in Curriculum Vitae Personal Website Blog Summary Varun Jindal is an Assistant Professor in the Finance and Accounting area at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, India. He holds a PhD in Finance and Control from the triple crown accredited Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Calcutta. Prior to pursuing PhD, he has served in the industry for close to 6 years in various roles, including but not limited to team management, strategic assistance to top management, software development, etc. His papers have been published (or accepted for publication) in the Journal of Corporate Finance , the British Accounting Review , the European Financial Management , and the International Business Review . He has also co-authored a case for IIM Calcutta Case Research Center. He has presented his research work at several leading international and national conferences. He is the recipient of several awards and honors including the Excellence in Teaching Awards at IIM Bangalore, the Distinguished Alumnus Award 2021 by Panjab University Alumni Association, the Springer Best Discussant Award at the Emerging Markets Conference 2021, Satish K. Sehgal Doctoral Student Award for Excellence in Scholarship and Organizational Citizenship 2020 at IIM Calcutta, the Emerald India Best Paper Award at the Pan IIM World Management Conference 2017, the Director’s Medal for the Best Outgoing Student of MBA Class of 2010, the CRISIL Young Thought Leader 2009 Runner-up Award, and the Knowledge Management Super Kruiser Award 2007 at Infosys Ltd. He is also a recipient of financial support of USD 3,750 for a policy paper under the NSE-NYU Stern Initiative on the Study of Indian Financial Markets 2018. Note: Professor Jindal is currently not accepting applications for internships. Accomplishments RESEARCH TEACHING AWARDS SERVICE EDUCATION RESEARCH INTERESTS: His research interest is in the broad area of empirical corporate finance, particularly in mergers and acquisitions and seasoned equity offerings. Read More >> About IIMB The Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) believes in building leaders through holistic, transformative and innovative education Read More >> Faculty profiles Srinivasan Rangan Home Faculty Srinivasan  Rangan Professor Finance & Accounting Chairperson, Finance & Accounting Connect with Faculty srinivasanr@iimb.ac.in Curriculum Vitae Personal Website Blog Summary Professor Rangan joined the Finance & Control Area of IIMB in May 2010. Earlier, he taught at Northwestern University, University of California at Davis, University of Colorado at Boulder, University of Texas at Dallas, Amrita School of Business (Coimbatore), and University of California at Berkeley. His work experience includes two years as a management consultant at Pricewaterhouse Coopers. Accomplishments RESEARCH TEACHING AWARDS EDUCATION His research interests are in the areas of market efficiency, financial analysis and valuation, initial public offerings, and earnings management. He has refereed publications in the Journal of Financial Economics, Accounting Review, Journal of Accounting Research, Review of Accounting Studies, and Financial Management . His work on earnings management and initial public offerings has been cited in The Wall Street Journal. Professor Rangan’s teaching interests include introductory and intermediate financial accounting, financial statement analysis, and stock valuation. Read More >> About IIMB The Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) believes in building leaders through holistic, transformative and innovative education Read More >> Faculty profiles Padmini Srinivasan Home Faculty Padmini  Srinivasan Professor Finance & Accounting Chairperson, Executive Education Programmes Chairperson, Centre for Corporate Governance and Sustainability Connect with Faculty padmini@iimb.ac.in Curriculum Vitae Personal Website Blog Summary Padmini Srinivasan has varied professional interests in teaching, research and consulting in the areas of Financial Reporting,  Management Accounting,  Corporate Governance and  accountability.  Prior to joining IIMB, she  worked in the  industry for more than 14 years in various positions in Treasury, Planning, MIS and Accounting. She is  also a special invitee to the Accounting standards Board of ICAI. Accomplishments RESEARCH TEACHING CONSULTING EDUCATION Her research interests are in the areas of Corporate governance and accountability, Corporate reporting and disclosures,  Value relevance of accounting numbers and Management Education Her recent research work are as follows: Srinivasan, P., & Bolar, P. (2020). Sustainability Risk Management: An Exploratory Study. IIM Bangalore Research Paper , (608). Marques, A. C., & Srinivasan, P. (2018). When corporate social responsibility is an obligation: the unique case of India. IIM Bangalore Research Paper Srinivasan P  and Srinivasan R (2015)  “Narrative Analysis of Annual Reports - A Study of Communication Efficiency” IIM Bangalore Research Paper No. 486 Srinivasan Padmini,  (2013),  “ An Analysis of Related Party Transactions in India”,  IIM Bangalore Research  paper No.   402 Srinivasan P and Narasimhan M.S., (2012) The Value Relevance of Consolidated Financial Statements in an Emerging Market: The Case of India"  Asian Review of Accounting,  Vol 20(1)  pages 58-73 Srinivasan, P., Srinivasan, V., & RV, Anand. (2012), “Status of Ethics, Corporate Governance, CSR and Environment Education in Business Schools in India: An Exploratory Study”, IIM Bangalore Research Paper , No: 362 Srinivasan P, “Now you see it, now you do not: The case of Jet Airways and its accounting policies”  2011,   IIMB  Case  through  Harvard Business Publishing Srinivasan P and  Narasimhan M.S. (2008),  “An Analysis of Consolidated and Parent-only Financial Statements of Indian Companies, The Indian Journal of Accounting Research and Audit Practices , Vol. 7(3),  27-42 As a full time  Faculty she teaches Financial Reporting and  Analysis,  Corporate Governance and ethics,  Management  Accounting,  and Corporate tax management in the Post Graduate Programs. Her teaching career includes in institutions including at the IIITB and National Law School of India, Bangalore. She was a visiting faculty at the University of Exeter Business School, UK She has designed and conducted programs for Executive Education including ‘Finance for Non-finance Executives’ for a number of companies. Sessions in these programs covered Financial Statement Analysis, IFRS, Working Capital Management, Cost Management and other Finance related topics including Equity Valuation . She has also designed and conducted programs on ‘Corporate Governance’ and Compliance for Senior Management and at the Board level. Professor Srinivasan has been consultant to many organizations and has experience in the areas of design and implementation of management information systems and, design of cost accounting and other corporate accounting systems. She was a member of the consulting team for the International Finance Corporation (World Bank) for their Bangalore Infrastructure Project. PhD, National Law School of India University, Bangalore Company Secretary, Associate Member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India Chartered Accountant, Fellow Member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India BCom, R.A. Podar College, Bombay University, India

His education includes PhD in Management Information Systems from IIM Calcutta, MBA from IIM Calcutta (including a semester at NEOMA Business School, France), and B.Tech in Computer Science & Engineering from NIT Durgapur. He has several years of practitioner experience at reputed technology companies like Microsoft, Computer Sciences Corporation (client: eBay), and Amazon. He has published in reputed journals like Journal of Management Information Systems (FT 50, ABDC A*), Decision Support Systems (ABDC A*), and Information & Management (ABDC A*). He has also won multiple prestigious awards and scholarships for his research. His research interests largely relate to conceptualizing and empirically observing human behavior in the context of contemporary technologies. His teaching philosophy is oriented towards providing state-of-the-art practical knowledge to serve the students interested in pursuing techno-management careers. Accordingly, he has designed courses on Digital Product Management, Information Systems, Emerging Technologies, etc. Accomplishments RESEARCH AWARDS SERVICE EDUCATION RESEARCH INTERESTS: Domain : Human psychology and behavior related to contemporary technologies and platforms having business applications Verticals : Virtual communities, Crowdfunding, Online reviews, E-commerce Methodology : Quantitative (Empirical, Experiments, Analytics & Machine Learning) JOURNAL PUBLICATIONS 1. Her current research interests include exploring, identifying, and resolving complex problems in the Human-Artificial Intelligence Collaboration and Health Informatics disciplines, using a combination of behavioral and analytical frameworks. Specifically, her most recent research models the collaboration between developers and bots in knowledge-intensive virtual communities like open-source software. In the healthcare informatics realm, her work on clinical trials for intelligent diagnostics has partly been funded by the Seattle Flu Study, Gates Ventures. Dr. Spurthy has presented her research at major international conferences in the IS area and Health Informatics, including DESRIST, AMCIS, and AMIA. With experience in using quantitative and qualitative research methodologies to design research studies, she led and co-authored publications in peer reviewed IS and health informatics journals. She also actively engages in practical service to her area of interest as a reviewer for several major IS conferences and journals. His work investigates the impact of digitization and technology adoption on human, social, and organizational relationships, and the strategic implications of these changes for organizations and society. Mayank's research has been published in top-tier journals, including Information Systems Journal, Journal of Knowledge Management, and International Journal of Information Management. He has also presented his research at prominent conferences such as ICIS and AMCIS and was selected for the prestigious ICIS Doctoral Consortium in 2018. Mayank's teaching expertise spans two key areas: newer digital technologies (Blockchain, IoT, Digital Platforms) and the intersection of technology and Marketing (Social Media Analytics, Digital Marketing, Data Visualization). Prior to joining IIM Bangalore, Mayank served as an Assistant Professor at IIT Jodhpur and MICA, Ahmedabad. At MICA, he played a significant role in administrative activities, leading the 'Digital Platform & Strategies' Area and serving on important committees such as Admissions and Doctoral Programme. As a founding faculty member of IIT Jodhpur's School of Management & Entrepreneurship, Mayank contributed significantly to institution-building activities, including curriculum design, MBA Admissions, and administrative tasks. Accomplishments RESEARCH EDUCATION Research Interests: Phenomenon: My research is broadly centred around examining the issues on the interaction of IT with the broader social and institutional structures such as power structures and work routines. Method: Methodologically, I am trained in qualitative approaches (e.g., Ethnography, Shadowing). Theories: As an interdisciplinary scholar, I draw upon the theories from Sociology and Organizational behavior in studying IS phenomenon. Prior to joining IIMB, Shankar worked in the IT industry around Cambridge, USA. At Sapient, he consulted with clients in energy and healthcare. He then moved to Curl Corporation, an MIT start-up, where he built bandwidth-efficient applets.  At Reuters Consulting, he worked with financial firms as a solutions architect. Shankar has strived to extend the reach of education with technology. He has anchored a program for school mathematics called Topper TV. His MOOCs on business statistics are featured on edX. As the IT Chair during the pandemic, he helped repurpose IIMB classrooms to reach students everywhere. Shankar is interested in data science, healthcare, and agile methods. He teaches courses in big data analytics and information systems management. He currently directs the DSAI program, which focuses on data science. He has created and directed the GMHE program, which is aimed at healthcare professionals. Shankar holds a doctorate in mathematics and a masters in computer science from Georgia Tech. His research interests include consumer emotion, motivation, scarcity, information processing, gift-giving, consumer receptivity to artificial intelligence, and retailing . He teaches courses on marketing management, marketing research, consumer behaviour and experimental design . He has over 15 years of teaching and research experience. His research works have been published in international journals such as Journal of Consumer Psychology , Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science , International Journal of Research in Marketing , Journal of Retailing , European Journal of Marketing , Psychology and Marketing , Journal of Business Research , and Journal of Services Marketing . He has extensive editorial experience and currently serves as an Associate Editor for the Journal of Business Research , European Journal of Marketing , and Psychology & Marketing . In addition, he is on the editorial board of the International Journal of Research in Marketing , the Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science , and the Journal of Services Marketing . Gopal is also a co-editor on a special issue on Scarcity for the Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science , on Retailing and Emergent Technologies for Journal of Business Research , and on Field Studies for European Journal of Marketing . He has received several recognitions/awards including featured in the World Top 2% list of researchers , ranked 2nd in the world in retailing journal influence index (2009-15) , Dipak C Jain award, and Outstanding Doctoral Management Student Award . He has been a Visiting Scholar of HKUST Business School, Hong Kong; and NUS Business School, Singapore. He has guided several Ph.D scholars. Accomplishments RESEARCH TEACHING CONSULTING EDUCATION RESEARCH INTEREST Consumer Receptivity to Artificial Intelligence; Consumer Emotion and Motivation; Scarcity; Information Processing; Gift-giving; and Retailing. PUBLICATION Gopal’s work has appeared in international journals such as Journal of Consumer Psychology , Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, International Journal of Research in Marketing , Journal of Retailing, Psychology & Marketing , European Journal of Marketing , Journal of Business Research, Journal of Services Marketing, and Journal of Business & Industrial Marketing . Gopal’s works have been presented at conferences such ACR, SCP, AMA, INFORMS, and EMAC. Through her research she aims to understand incentive structures that drive buyer/seller behavior and functioning of markets. Her recent work includes structuring and framing prices for digital, technology, and agri-markets. Her work has been published in leading journals such as Management Science, Manufacturing & Service Operations Management, and the IIM B Management Review. She held IIMB chair of Excellence, 2016-2019. Professor Jonnalagedda has worked on case studies/consulting engagements on pricing and marketing innovations, including pricing information products such as InMobi, Red Force Labs, and Amable. Most recently she has consulted with the Tea Board of India for restructuring tea auctions. Professor Jonnalagedda holds a PhD from The University of Texas, Austin, Master of Science from the New Jersey Institute of Technology, and Bachelor of Technology from the Indian Institute of Technology, Madras. Prior to completing her Ph.D., she worked as a consultant with Supply Chain Consultants, Inc (now Arkieva). She completed her PhD in Marketing from IIM Ahmedabad, where her dissertation on consumer behavior in online cause-related marketing received the best thesis award. Her research interests lie in the domains of digital marketing, advertising, sustainable consumption and consumer behavior. Her work has been published in leading international journals, including the Journal of Marketing Research, Journal of Service Research and International Journal of Advertising . Her teaching includes advanced marketing courses on Strategies for Mobile Marketing. Prior to joining the PhD programme at IIMA, she worked for two years in Accenture Management Consulting. She completed her MBA from IIT Kanpur where she was awarded the S N Mittal Gold Medal for all round excellence in the graduating batch. title: Chicago Booth-India Quantitative Marketing Conference, 17th December 2018, IIM Bangalore
text: Chicago Booth-India Quantitative Marketing Conference, 17th December 2018, IIM Bangalore About IIMB Programmes Research Faculty Center of Excellence Executive Education Journal MOOCS Resources Research Support WE'RE HIRING Blog Alumni Research Support WE'RE HIRING Blog Alumni FAQ About IIMB Programmes Research Faculty Executive Education Center of Excellence Journal MOOCS IIMB > Chicago Booth-India Quantitative Marketing Conference, 17th December 2018, IIM Bangalore Chicago Booth-India Quantitative Marketing Conference, 17th December 2018, IIM Bangalore Chicago Booth-India Quantitative Marketing Conference, 2018 17th December, 2018, IIMB Welcome to the Chicago Booth-India Quantitative Marketing conference to be held at IIM Bangalore on Dec 17th, 2018. The University of Chicago established a center in Delhi to serve as a base for research, teaching and dialogue among scholars from the University, across India and around the world. With the express purpose of building research relationships with faculty in India, The Booth School of Business at the university launched a mini-conference in quantitative marketing in 2017 at the Delhi Center. This year the conference is being held at IIM Bangalore, with research presentations from faculty based in India. Location IIM Bangalore, Opposite Apollo Hospital, Bannerghatta Rd Bangalore : 560076 For information on how to get to the campus, visit the directions to IIMB link . Conference Room Location N001. Conference attendees can reach the main reception area to seek guidance to the conference room. Contact IIMB’s main phone extension +91-2699 - 3000 for more information. Please check the below map for directions Schedule Chicago Booth India Quantitative Marketing Conference Dec 17th 2018, @IIM Bangalore, Room N001 Presenting AT By On From 8:40 AM - 9:00 AM Pradeep Chintagunta & Sanjog Misra Introduction/Coffee/Meet Greet U Chicago 9:00 AM - 9:50 AM Sreelata Jonnalagedda Can critics continue to be critical? Evidence from the movie industry IIM Bangalore 10:00 AM - 10:50 AM Prithwiraj Mukherji Social Media Advertising and Fake Followers IIM Bangalore 10:50 AM to 11:20 AM COFFEE BREAK 11:20 AM - 11:50 AM Anusha Gondi An analysis of market value and product-market Choices ISB 11:50 AM - 12:50 PM Vedha Ponappan Should manufacturers pass through sugar tax or reformulate their products? IIM Bangalore 12:50 PM to 02:00 PM LUNCH(MDC) 02:00 PM - 02:50 PM Manaswini Bhalla Information flows, familiarity bias, and M & A outcomes IIM Bangalore 03:00 PM - 03:50 PM Aruna Divya Pricing upgrades and cross-sells when consumers experience regret IIM Ahmedabad 03:50 PM to 04:10 PM COFFEE BREAK 04:10 PM - 04:40 PM Shiv Saini Sparse forecasting for time series decomposition and anomaly detection Adobe 04:40 PM - 05:10 PM Priya Narayanan Monetary impact of customer familiarity and cart variables in online shopping IIM Ahmedabad 05:10 PM - 05:30 PM High Tea/ General Discussion Networking Closing Comments Presentations Can Critics Continue to be Critical? Evidence from the Movie Industry Presenter:Sreelata Jonnalagedda, IIM Bangalore Abstract: Availability of composite ratings on e-aggregators and the touting of these ratings by the movie studios as part of the movie’s advertising campaigns have brought to question the role of individual critics in influencing the movie’s box office performance. In this study, we examine whether e-aggregators have overshadowed the impact of individual critics on movie’s box office performance. Collaborators: Ashish Kumar, Aalto School of Busines; Mauli Soni, IIM Bangalore Social Media Advertising and Fake Followers Presenter:Prithwiraj Mukherjee, IIM Bangalore Abstract: Marketing promotions via paid social media influencers are now commonplace across the world. These influencers are minor celebrities with self-selected audiences based on their domains of interest, and often make thousands of dollars per sponsored post. However, this practice has led to the emergence of click farms - businesses that sell fake followers to such influencers to artificially inflate their follower counts, thus signaling higher reach and thus more fees from advertisers using their services. In this paper, we develop an optimal contract between an influencer and advertiser that maximizes advertiser profit given that the influencer can buy fake followers from click farms. Collaborators: Abhinav Anand & Souvik Dutta, IIM Bangalore An Analysis of Market Value and Product-Market Choices Presenter:Anusha Gondi, ISB Hyderabad Abstract: We empirically examine two quantities of interest in Marketing and Strategy research, namely, Market Value - the firm's capitalized market value as a summary measure of investor belief in the firm's future profits, and product-market choices - the firm's scope of activities and operations across distinct product-markets. Collaborators: Sudhir Voleti, ISB Hyderabad Sugar Tax: Should Manufacturers Pass Through Sugar Tax or Reformulate Products Presenter:Vedha Ponappan, IIM Bangalore Abstract: We examine manufacturer’s optimal response strategy to a policy interventions such as sugar tax, by first investigating consumer’s potential response to a sugar tax or product reformulation. We use a direct utility based structural model that incorporates product characteristics to recover consumer’s intrinsic preferences for various product attributes. Using a multiple discrete continuous choice framework, we also recover consumers’ variety seeking preferences and the strength of their preference to the focal category compared to other categories based on their past purchases. Collaborators: Srinivas Prakhya, IIM Bangalore Directors of a Feather Merge Together: Information Flows, Familiarity Bias, M & A Outcomes Presenter: Manaswini Bhalla, IIM Bangalore Abstract: We show that cultural proximity between two firms boards leads to a higher likelihood of the two firms entering a merger and acquisition (M & A) deal in India. This phenomenon may indicate firms' reliance on culture, as measured by caste, as an informal channel of information when making critical investment decisions with imperfect information. However, it may also be driven by familiarity bias leading to sub-optimal investments. Indeed, caste-proximate M & A deals are value destroying for both acquirer and target, as well as the merged entity. Overall, our findings show that familiarity bias in favor of culturally proximate agents can lead to sub-optimal investment decisions. Collaborators: Manisha Goel & Michelle Zemel, Pomona College; VSK Teja Konduri, IIM Bangalore Pricing Upgrades and Cross-sells when Consumers Experience Regret Presenter : Aruna Divya Tatavarthy, IIM Ahmedabad Abstract: When consumers experience regret associated with an under-consumed service, how do add-ons help consumers recover lost value? Does the pricing of add-on and recovery of value depend on the price structure of the base service? In this research, we examine a firm’s add-on pricing strategy as a function of the extent of add-on complementary and the regret compensation mechanism employed by consumers, under two base-price structures: a) pay-per-use and b) fixed-fee pricing structure. Collaborators: Sreelata Jonnalagedda, IIM Bangalore Sparse Forecasting for Time Series Decomposition and Anomaly Detection Presenter : Shiv Kumar Saini, Adobe Systems Abstract: Common examples of limiting assumptions in time series analysis  include perfect knowledge about the time series seasonality and/or presence of anomaly (spikes and level changes) free time windows. Current practice is to manually input this knowledge into anomaly detection and forecasting systems which negate any possibility of autonomous analysis. This paper relaxes these assumptions by jointly estimating the latent components (viz. seasonality, level changes, and spikes) in the observed time series without assuming the availability of anomaly-free time windows. Collaborators: Sunav Choudary, Adobe Systems; Gaurush Hiranandani, UIUC Monetary Impact of Customer Familiarity and Cart Variables in Online Shopping Presenter : Priya Narayanan, IIM Ahmedabad Abstract: Our research has two main objectives. The first is to determine the impact of the path followed by the consumer during online shopping on the revenue generated from purchases. The second is to determine the impact of variables related to the consumer and to the cart on amount paid for the cart. We study the first question in the context of 342,713 shopping sessions recorded over a single day, leading to 3002 separate product purchases. Similarly, we study the second question in the context of 3056 converted shopping carts on a single day. He has held senior management roles leading the HRM, Talent Development & OD, Management Services, and Corporate Communication Departments, working with MNCs and large private and public sector organizations. In his corporate and consulting career, he has institutionalized multiple processes and built-in focus for vision, culture, talent, values, and growth for many of these organizations. During his corporate and consulting career, along with his crucial role in business, Prof. Gopal has retained his commitment to academic involvement by taking up teaching engagements in top Business schools and professional bodies, including the IIMs, and conducting courses in the areas of Leadership, Talent Management, TQM, Mentoring and Coaching, Change Management, Performance Management, Assessment Development Centers, and Strategic HR. Since August 2018, working as a Professor of Practice, OB & HRM at IIM Bengaluru, he has been teaching courses on Leadership in Digital Era, Managing People and Performance in Organisation, Managing Career Success and Transitions, Executive Coaching and Mentoring for Full- time and Part-time MBA students and executives, in addition to teaching various Leadership, Career Success and Change Management related MDP sessions. He was also the Chairman of PGPEM, a weekend MBA course supporting working professionals pursuing MBA during weekends to enhance their competencies and readiness for the future. Active in the functioning of many not-for-profit organizations and academic bodies, he has served as President of the National HRD Network, Bangalore, Academic Council Member of Reserve Bank of India Staff College, PDEU, MICA , XIM Univ SHRM, Chinmaya Viswa Vidyapeeth, KIIT SOM, and leading B-Schools, Trustee of Gomasu Development Foundation, Adviser to a Social Entrepreneurial Startup and Founding Associate Editor of South Asian Journal of HRM published by Sage since 2013 and since 2018 Sage NHRDN Journal and a Springer invited Editor book on Business cases in OB &HRM. He is acknowledged in business and academic forums as an HR Thought Leader, Leadership Coach, and a successful Organizational Transformation Practitioner passionate about building Institutions and establishing systems to enhance performance, bringing about system efficacies. He has a B.Tech. from IIT Kanpur, MBA from IIM Calcutta and PhD in Decision Sciences from INSEAD, France. His research interest is in behavioral decision making. He has published in leading academic journals like PNAS, Psychological Review, Management Science, Psychological Science, Journal of Behavioral Decision Making and Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory and Cognition.  He is a recipient of the Hillel Einhorn Award from the Society of Judgment and Decision Making and his research has been featured extensively in various press and media outlets. He won the “Lifestyle for Environment” (LiFE) Global Call for Ideas & Papers, a sustainability effort launched by India’s PM, Shri Narendra Modi at COP26, Glasgow. He has also consulted for the Government of India on policy matters of national importance. His current research involves large scale field studies on reducing energy use in airconditioned hotel rooms as well as a multiyear study on inducing water conservation behavior in households. He is also exploring how Gen AI affects group dynamics. His research interests include strategic sourcing, operational issues in cloud computing, management of digital technologies, smart city operations, urban mobility, and pricing issues in service supply chains. His work has been published in journals such as Production and Operations Management, IISE Transactions, Naval Research Logistics, Decision Sciences, Service Science, European Journal of Operational Research, IEEE Transactions on Engineering Management, Journal of Product Innovation Management, Journal of Operational Research Society, PLOS One, Journal of Revenue and Pricing Management and International Journal of Production Economics. Haritha’s research interests include studying quality, productivity and sustainability aspects of firms operating in agricultural, automotive, pharmaceutical and healthcare supply chains in India and abroad. She uses both empirical and analytical methods in her research, including data envelopment analysis, multiple regression, Time series, panel data and optimization. Haritha Saranga is a Fellow of MIRCE Akademy, Exeter, UK. She has published several articles in refereed international journals, such as Production and Operations Management , Journal of International Business Studies, European Journal of Operational Research, MIT Sloan Management Review and Journal of Operational Research Society . She also co-authored a book, titled Reliability and Six Sigma , published by Springer and has written many cases and book chapters. His research explores how insights from economics and psychology can be applied to understand and influence behaviour of individuals or groups. His research has applications in several areas including sustainability in the lower-tiers of supply chains, online retail, healthcare, and other areas of consequential decision making. He holds a PhD in Quantitative Methods and Operations Management from the Indian Institute of Management Kozhikode. His work has been published in journals such as International Journal of Production Research. Prior to pursuing PhD, he served as Operations Officer in Indian Oil Corporation Ltd for 3.5 years. Accomplishments RESEARCH EDUCATION Research Interests: His research interests are in the areas of behavioural operations, sustainable supply chains, online retail, and applications of neuro science in business. He has a refereed publication in the International Journal of Production Research. His academic and professional interests lie at the intersection of sustainable operations, game theory, and supply chain economics. He teaches across IIM Bangalore’s MBA and doctoral programs, offering courses on Game Theory, Responsible Business Operations, and Operations Management. His excellence in teaching has been recognized within the institution. His research has been published in top-tier journals such as the European Journal of Operational Research, Journal of the Operational Research Society, and Operations Research Letters, and has received best paper awards at multiple academic conferences. Prior to academia, Rajeev worked with Ford Motor Company as part of the Global Data Insights and Analytics group, where he focused on advanced operational analytics, smart mobility, and enterprise risk. Read More >> About IIMB The Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) believes in building leaders through holistic, transformative and innovative education Read More >> Faculty profiles Nilam Kaushik Home Faculty Nilam  Kaushik Assistant Professor Strategy Connect with Faculty nilam.kaushik@iimb.ac.in Curriculum Vitae Personal Website Blog Summary Dr. Nilam Kaushik is an Assistant Professor in Strategy at Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB). She earned her PhD from the UCL School of Management in London, England in 2019.  She received her Bachelors in Communications Engineering from Carleton University in Ottawa, Canada in 2007 and pursued her Master’s degree in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the University of Waterloo. Dr. Kaushik was recognised among the “Best 40 Under 40 MBA Professors” by Poets and Quants in 2023. She is the first Professor from an Indian Business school to receive this recognition.  In 2024 she has also received the “Young Woman Researcher In Innovation Management” award at the 9th Venus International Women Awards. Prior to pursuing her doctoral studies, she worked as a Software Developer at BlackBerry (formerly Research In Motion) and has a patent to her credit from her work there. During her time as a doctoral student, she was also a Visiting Scholar at the D’Amore-McKim School of Business at Northeastern University from 2016 to 2017. Dr. Nilam Kaushik’s interests lie broadly in innovation and entrepreneurship. In her work, she combines interdisciplinary methods and techniques such as text-mining, information retrieval and econometrics, and also uses field experiments. She is a Research Affiliate of the IoT Open Innovation Lab at Northeastern University and continues to be an Honorary Research Associate at the UCL School of Management.
